content:
周四，中国、美国和俄罗斯总统在首次三边峰会前与其他亚太领导人合影留念，北京称这次峰会是关于“世界和平”的会谈。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会上，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（左）在领导人合影前合影。照片：Greg Baker/法新社。习近平、特朗普和普京在深圳麒麟山庄举行三方会晤之际，俄罗斯对乌克兰的血腥攻势已接近五年。因中期选举失败而受伤的特朗普又因与伊朗的战争而陷入困境，而崛起的中国正在寻求加强其在东亚的影响力。这次秘密会议引发了人们的担忧，担心这三位有权势的人可能会寻求将全球划分为势力范围，例如将乌克兰的命运凌驾于基辅或欧洲之上。此前，特朗普和习近平将举行双边讨论，预计将讨论贸易关系以及英伟达间谍丑闻笼罩下的人工智能潜在共同规则。北京、华盛顿和莫斯科对亚太经合组织(APEC)论坛期间的会议内容给出了不同的描述。在特朗普表示战争将成为焦点之前，华盛顿最初表示不考虑乌克兰问题。
习近平并不认为这场冲突是中国需要解决的问题。克里姆林宫表示，议程尚未最终确定，但在会议上很难避免讨论乌克兰问题，会议预计将持续“不超过一个小时”。 2026 年 5 月 20 日，孩子们在北京人民大会堂举行的欢迎仪式上向中国国家主席习近平（左）和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京致意。照片：克里姆林宫。自 2022 年发动全面进攻以来，普京在很大程度上受到西方大国的回避，他在周三的亚太经合组织会议上表示，西方对其国家的制裁“失败了”。 “在军事政治风险上升之际，迫切需要的是……对话而不是最后通牒，”他说。中国仅表示，三方将“就维护世界和平、促进大国关系战略稳定进行深入交流”。批评者警告说，这次会议的景象将对美国总统造成损害。参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默表示：“习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京就像演奏廉价小提琴一样演奏唐纳德·特朗普。”盛大的欢迎 根据华盛顿的说法，在美俄双边原子武器条约二月份到期后，伊朗战争和核裁军问题也将成为讨论的焦点。然而，北京长期以来一直坚持认为，美国和俄罗斯应该先削减其庞大的核武库，然后才同意就其较小的核武库进行谈判。 “看，我们有 4000 件核武器。
俄罗斯拥有 3,800 枚核武器。中国现在有四五百枚，但他们会赶上的。你知道，在十年的时间里，他们正在行动。”特朗普告诉福克斯新闻。特朗普表示，他还考虑与普京以及朝鲜领导人金正恩进行一对一会谈，尽管后者没有出席会议。朝鲜领导人金正恩（左）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（右）。照片：白宫/Flickr。习近平在

【原文 English Original】
The presidents of China, the United States and Russia posed for a photo with other Asia-Pacific leaders on Thursday ahead of their first ever trilateral summit, billed by Beijing as talks about “world peace”. China’s President Xi Jinping (R) and US President Donald Trump (L) pose for a photo before leaders take a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: Greg Baker/AFP. The three-way meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen comes with Russia’s bloody offensive in Ukraine approaching the five-year mark. Trump, wounded by the midterm election debacle, is bogged down by his war with Iran, and an ascendant China is looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. The conclave has stoked fears that the three powerful men may seek to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example deciding the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Beforehand Trump and Xi were due to hold bilateral discussions expected to touch on trade ties and potentially common rules for AI under the cloud of the Nvidia spy scandal . Beijing, Washington and Moscow have given different accounts of what they expect to discuss from the powwow on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. The Kremlin has said that the agenda had not been finalised, but it would be hard to avoid discussing Ukraine at the meeting, which is set to last “no more than an hour”. Children greet Chinese President Xi Jinping (left) and Russian President Vladimir Putin during the welcome ceremony at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 20, 2026. Photo: The Kremlin. Putin, largely shunned by Western powers since his 2022 full-scale offensive, told the APEC gathering on Wednesday that Western sanctions on his country had “failed”. “At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is… dialogue rather than ultimatums,” he said. China has said only that the trio will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting will be damaging for the US president. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said. Lavish welcome Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. However, Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. “Look, we have 4,000 nuclear weapons. Russia has 3,800 nuclear weapons. China now has four or five hundred, but they’re going to catch (up). You know, over a 10-year period, they’re moving,” Trump told Fox News. Trump has said he is also eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin as well as North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though the latter is not present at the conference. North Korean Leader Kim Jong-un (left) and US President Donald Trump (right). Photo: The White House/Flickr. In a sign of the importance that China is placing on the trilateral summit, Xi gave Trump an extravagant welcome on Wednesday. Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, the Chinese leader personally received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air-force flyover. It was the first time that China’s paramount leader had welcomed a foreign dignitary in person for decades, and reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September. “It’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship,” Trump told Fox News from Shenzhen. Xi “has never gone to the airport to meet somebody… It was a great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China too,” Trump said. ‘Serene authority’ “I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. In contrast, Putin was welcomed at the airport by Cai Qi, China’s fifth-ranked leader, in accordance with regular protocol. Other world leaders at the APEC meeting include Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, South Korea’s Lee Jae Myung, Canada’s Mark Carney and Australia’s Anthony Albanese. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (left) and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, on October 31, 2025. Photo: Sanae Takaichi, via X. Takaichi, on her first visit to China since angering Beijing a year ago with comments about Taiwan, met Putin — with whom relations are also tense — on Wednesday, Tokyo said. Despite their differences, all the leaders — including Putin — posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in matching scarves. Apart from the centrepiece trilateral, the group was also expected to discuss a range of other topics, including trade policy and artificial intelligence. Xi opened the APEC leaders’ meeting on Thursday with a call to “reduce barriers to trade and investment”. Analysts believe the day’s events will be heavily scripted, but underline that the personalities may yet spring surprises. “Typically, when Chinese leaders host meetings, every detail is nailed down and China’s leader is positioned to project an air of serene authority and control,” said Ryan Hass at the Brookings Institution. “Given the other leaders involved though — Trump and Putin — there is only so much choreography that can be done to eliminate unexpected moments,” Hass told AFP.

title: Anatomy of a Chinese loanbook

summary: ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ 数据团队剖析了 200 多个贷款机构
content:
ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ数据团队剖析了2010年至2024年期间的200多份贷款协议和修正案。ICIJ发现，在审查的协议和修正案中，工银伦敦至少与另一家中国国有商业银行合作。在中国的银行中，中国银行脱颖而出，成为工银伦敦分行的主要中方合作伙伴：双方签署了 102 项协议。 ICIJ 的分析显示，这家中国银行业巨头的伦敦分行通常与其他中国和国际银行合作，达成价值数亿美元甚至更多的贷款协议。 ICIJ 发现了 36 项贷款协议和修正案，其中一半或以上的资金是由中国贷方提供的。其中 16 个案例的财务承诺完全来自中资银行。
ICIJ 的一项审查发现，作为对该行客户尽职调查过程的一部分，中国工商银行准备的文件显示，该行有时会淡化合规问题，或以其他方式证明继续与其被归类为高风险的客户开展业务是合理的。 在赞比亚，中国工商银行在加剧该国债务负担、造成对中国贷款的依赖以及给赞比亚人造成多年困难方面发挥了作用。在英国，中国工商银行的银行管理人员无视其一位中国客户在美国法院面临的法律风险，以便该银行能够为该公司收购英国竞争对手并巩固其市场份额提供资金。下面的案例研究揭示了一家银行在中国党国议程的推进与其自身的全球商业野心之间取得平衡的内部运作方式。无视红灯 01 2024年5月，工商银行的高风险客户名单包括全球燃料贸易商和分销商Puma Energy的融资部门以及大股东Trafigura Pte.有限公司是一家注册并总部位于新加坡的贸易巨头，主要贸易业务位于瑞士，以及另外两家托克实体。尽管中国工商银行对 Puma 和 Trafigura 的担忧至少可以追溯到 2015 年，但 ICIJ 发现 2015 年至 2024 年间涉及 Puma 和 Trafigura 的 19 项银团信贷安排协议，总价值达 387 亿美元。 ICBC 的伦敦实体在这些贷款中总共承诺提供 14 亿美元。
2015年，工商银行加大了对Puma旗下融资工具Puma International Financing的尽职调查力度；在其2015年5月的强化尽职调查（EDD）报告中，将该公司的贿赂风险评为“高”。 当时，Puma的股东包括安哥拉国有石油公司Sonangol和Cochan Holdings LLC（一家由安哥拉总统顾问Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento创立并担任主席的投资公司）。该报告承认，媒体广泛报道了涉及安哥拉高级官员的贿赂和腐败行为，其中包括当时的总统若泽·爱德华多·多斯桑托斯及其子女，以及Sonangol、Cochan和Nascimento。尽管如此，工行仍对大部分逆回购进行了描述

【原文 English Original】
ICIJ’s China Capital investigation revealed how the London units of the world’s largest bank, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), routinely financed companies to push Beijing’s geopolitical agenda, sometimes flouting their own compliance rules in the process. ICIJ, in collaboration with 23 media partners, obtained 4.8 million internal documents leaked from ICBC London, including loan application forms, due diligence reports, know-your-client documents and internal email exchanges. To better understand ICBC’s London operations, the ICIJ data team dissected more than 200 loan agreements and amendments dated from 2010 to 2024. ICIJ found that ICBC London partnered with at least one other Chinese state-owned commercial bank in more than half of the agreements and amendments reviewed. Among the Chinese lenders, Bank of China stands out as the main Chinese partner of ICBC London: They joined forces in 102 agreements. ICIJ’s analysis shows that the London units of the Chinese banking giant usually partnered with other Chinese and international banks on loan agreements often worth hundreds of millions of dollars—or more. ICIJ identified 36 loan agreements and amendments for which half or more of the money was provided by Chinese lenders. In 16 of those cases, the financial commitments were entirely from Chinese banks. ICBC documents prepared as part of the due diligence process on the bank’s clients show how the bank at times downplayed compliance problems or otherwise justified continued business with clients it had classified as high risk, an ICIJ review found. In Zambia, ICBC played a role in exacerbating the country’s debt burden, creating dependency on Chinese loans and contributing to years-long difficulties for Zambians. In the U.K., ICBC bank officers disregarded legal risks faced in a U.S. court by one of their Chinese clients so the bank could finance the company’s acquisition of a British competitor and consolidate its market share. The case studies below reveal the inner workings of a bank balancing the advancement of the agenda of the Chinese party-state with its own global commercial ambitions. Ignoring Red Lights 01 In May 2024, ICBC’s high-risk client list included the financing arm of global fuel trader and distributor Puma Energy, along with a major shareholder Trafigura Pte. Ltd., a trading giant registered and headquartered in Singapore with major trading operations in Switzerland, and two other Trafigura entities. Despite ICBC's concerns about Puma and Trafigura dating back to at least 2015, ICIJ identified 19 syndicated credit facility agreements involving Puma and Trafigura, between 2015 and 2024, with a combined value of $38.7 billion. ICBC's London entities committed a total of $1.4 billion across those facilities. In 2015, ICBC escalated its due diligence of Puma’s financing vehicle, Puma International Financing; in its May 2015 Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) report, it rated the company’s bribery risk as high. At the time, Puma's shareholders included Angola's state-owned oil company Sonangol and Cochan Holdings LLC, an investment company founded and chaired by Angolan presidential adviser Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento. The report acknowledged extensive adverse media coverage alleging bribery and corruption involving senior Angolan officials, including then-President José Eduardo dos Santos and his children, as well as Sonangol, Cochan and Nascimento. Still, ICBC characterized much of the adverse reporting as “rumour based and unfounded” and continued the relationship, subject to enhanced monitoring. In February 2020, ICBC’s EDD report again identified allegations centered on Nascimento’s close ties to former President dos Santos and speculation in media reports and elsewhere that he had used political connections to acquire a stake in Puma Energy while serving as a public official. The report also noted that Nascimento had faced investigations into alleged corruption, conflicts of interest and money laundering in several countries. Yet ICBC cited reasons for discounting the risks, noting that Nascimento did “not appear to have been convicted” of wrongdoing. In December 2021, the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Nascimento and Cochan, saying Nascimento and another Angolan official had embezzled billions from the Angolan government. In 2025, an Angolan court convicted Nascimento of fraud, document forgery, money laundering and influence peddling. Likewise, ICBC's October 2019 Enhanced Due Diligence report came after a highly public Brazilian corruption investigation into allegations that commodity traders, including Trafigura, had bribed employees of Petrobras, Brazil’s state-owned and state-controlled oil company. A month earlier, Reuters reported allegations that senior Trafigura executives Mike Wainwright and José Larocca knew about the bribes. But ICBC's EDD report referred only to "two high-ranking executives” at Trafigura, without identifying them, despite separately listing both men as key controllers of Trafigura. Wainwright's adverse-media assessment was marked "No." ICBC continued the relationship, citing Trafigura's status as a longstanding "strategic client," the participation of major international banks in syndicated loans, its compliance controls and the absence of suspicious activity detected by ICBC. In 2024, Trafigura Beheer B.V., the Dutch-registered former parent company of the Trafigura Group, pleaded guilty in the U.S. to conspiring to violate U.S. anti-bribery laws in a scheme that ran from approximately 2003 to 2014. The companies also reached a settlement agreement with Brazilian authorities. Read responses Responses Trafigura: In response to ICIJ's questions, a Trafigura spokesperson said lender due diligence was a normal part of doing business and that the company cooperated with lenders' reviews, supported by its public financial and sustainability disclosures. Regarding the Petrobras bribery case, the spokesperson referred to Trafigura's 2024 statement announcing the resolution of the U.S. investigation, in which the company said the misconduct involved former employees or agents and was inconsistent with its principles and code of conduct. The statement said U.S. authorities had recognized improvements to Trafigura's anti-corruption compliance procedures. Puma: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Nascimento: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Angolan government: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Cochan: ICIJ could not successfully contact Cochan for comment. Sonangol: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. A legal representative for Mike Wainwright didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. José Larocca: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Puma International Financing S.A., Trafigura Group Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Trading LLC Amount $1.4 billionTotal loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2024 From the China Capital files PUMA In their own words: There is a wealth of adverse news in the public domain citing the Angolan Government's bribery and corruption and monopolisation of various industries in Angola.Risk From the China Capital files TRAFIGURA In their own words: The risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened [...] and thus this poses an increased reputational risk to the Bank.Risk Trafigura is an existing and strategic client of the Bank.Mitigating factors Financing Kleptocrats 02 ICBC started lending to Socar, Azerbaijan’s state oil and gas concern, in 2015 when ICBC London took part in a revolving credit facility to one of the company’s subsidiaries, Socar Trading SA. Even though the bank decided to exit this facility in 2019 because of the company's “underperformance and ongoing restructuring," a review of ICBC documents shows that under the head office’s encouragement, ICBC’s London and Turkey offices maintained close connection with Socar. Bank officers in an internal memo noted “Azerbaijan's geopolitical importance in the area's political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors,” adding “SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China's 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy." ICBC London committed to at least three additional loans, each between $25 million and $89 million, even as the bank continued to list Socar among high-risk clients, with one document stating: “the risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened." Corporate bank officers underlined the risks presented by the nature of Socar’s business and its jurisdiction, Azerbaijan; the fact that all the members of its board of directors were, at the time, identified as politically exposed persons, including the president and 12 vice presidents; Socar’s lack of transparency and accountability; and that the company had recently featured in major international corruption scandals. Yet the same year that ICBC listed these risks, 2021, the bank agreed to lend Socar $89 million. ICBC and Socar had deepened their ties in 2018, when the bank’s London branch listed $1.58 billion worth of green bonds on the London Stock Exchange, and Azerbaijan's State Oil Fund, SOFAZ, decided to invest $150 million. Socar, which sells oil and gas on the state’s behalf, contributed about 90% of SOFAZ’s 2017 revenue. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project later reported that leaked documents from inside British Petroleum exposed that two Socar subsidiaries were set to siphon off more than $1.7 billion from the Shah Deniz 2 gas project through padded contracts and fake charges. Socar denied the allegations. Read response Response Socar: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. SOFAZ: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrower Socar and its subsidiaries Amount $217 million (4 loans)Total loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2021 From the China Capital files In their own words: Given Azerbaijan’s geopolitical importance in the area’s political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors, SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China’s 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy aimed at creating infrastructure and establishing links among the Eurasian countries.Risk Consolidating Market Share 03 ICBC records show bank risk management officials looking past the potentially illegal actions of a Chinese customer seeking a loan to buy out one of its competitors. In 2017 ICBC London Branch agreed to back China’s Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.’s acquisition of Sepura PLC, a British telecommunications competitor in the mobile radio communications sector. Hytera designs and manufactures professional mobile communications devices commonly used by law enforcement agencies worldwide — including two-way radios, a market that at the time was expected to be worth $7.3 billion by 2025. The agreement with ICBC London, which was the only lender involved, allowed Hytera to borrow up to $57.1 million over three years. Sepura shareholders had approved the $92.7 million acquisition in January 2017 but antitrust authorities in the UK and Germany, where governments relied on Sepura’s technology, stalled the acquisition. Spanish antitrust authorities also assessed the transaction, which was eventually approved in May of that year. While conducting their due diligence work to approve the loan in early 2017, ICBC London employees discovered that Motorola Solutions Inc., another competitor in the mobile telecommunications market, had filed a lawsuit pending against Hytera in a U.S. federal court for alleged patent infringement and industrial espionage. The bank’s compliance officers allowed the loan to go forward anyway, adding a handwritten note on a printout of an article about the suit that the case wasn’t related to any major financial crime. The article mentioned, however, that Motorola accused Hytera of hiring ex-Motorola employees after they had allegedly stolen thousands of pages of confidential documents. By early 2020, while Hytera was repaying the loan ICBC employees flagged a problem — Hytera had lost its U.S. case. In a briefing note to the bank’s credit committee at the end of April, they wrote that the verdict “confirms that Hytera engaged in illegal trade secret theft and copyright infringement, validating Motorola's global litigation against Hytera.” Following the U.S. court verdict ICBC London received an injunction from a British court ordering the bank to freeze Hytera assets, potentially stopping the repayment of the loan. Seven Hytera employees were later indicted for their alleged roles in the thefts from Motorola; one pleaded guilty in 2022 to charges of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and is awaiting sentencing. Hytera pleaded guilty in 2025 to “conspiracy to steal trade secrets” and was fined $50 million. Hytera was also ordered to pay Motorola more than $400 million in a separate lawsuit. In 2021, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission published a list of Chinese manufacturers, including Hytera, which “pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States.” The same year, the British government passed the National Security and Investment Act which gave heightened power to the government to proactively review acquisitions in 17 sensitive sectors, including communications. Hytera sold its entire shareholding in Sepura in July 2022. Read responses Responses Hytera: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In an email to ICIJ, Sepura said that "neither Sepura PLC nor its shareholders or management at the time were involved in Hytera’s choice of funding for its acquisition of Sepura” and that the company “had no customer relationship with ICBC and held no accounts with the bank” following the acquisition. It also said that it was not “a party to the litigation brought by Motorola against Hytera concerning Motorola’s intellectual property” and that “the technology at issue was distinct from that developed and used by Sepura in its own products”. “Sepura's proprietary technology and IPR were ring-fenced by statutory undertakings, as mandated and defined by the UK government and accepted by Hytera.” Sepura said it “has had no further interaction with Hytera since the sale” in 2022. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Borrower Project Shortway Ltd. (ultimately owned by Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.) Amount up to $57.1 millionTotal loan commitments Start date of loans May 2017 From the China Capital files In their own words Handwritten note on an article: Not major financial crime issues relatedRisk Buying your backyard 04 ICBC participated in syndicated loans — financing provided by a group of lenders who share the risk — for a Chinese commercial real estate venture that went bust and defaulted on its loans, according to internal loan agreements and property assessments reviewed by ICIJ. In 2017, Chinese real estate tycoon Chen Hongtian and his wife bought two office towers in London’s trendy Canary Wharf commercial district, hoping to convert their $900 million investment into a profitable venture. ICBC London described the area as “one of the world’s premier commercial districts,” with “24 office buildings with around 200 shops, bars, and restaurants” according to a 2022 assessment of 5 Churchill Place’s value by the real estate company managing the asset. The real estate firm’s assessment came as the bank and other creditors looked to liquidate the assets of the embattled tycoon who had found himself short on cash and unable to make payments. By then, ICBC London Branch had committed $205 million out of roughly half a billion in loans made with other banks to Chen’s companies in the British Virgin Islands, through which he and his family owned the London properties. One of those properties, at 20 Canada Square, was mainly occupied by two Western firms, according to a 2022 ICBC internal credit report. But the properties couldn’t compete with more modern and energy-efficient real estate, and their value plummeted. By April 2023 ICBC London had reclassified the loan to Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., a BVI company through which Chen owned some units of the Canada Square property, as “non performing” and added the borrower to its watchlist. Around the same time that ICBC was reviewing the properties, the UK government passed the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act which required overseas entities that hold property in England and Wales to file beneficial ownership information with the company registry. A report published in 2017 by the U.S. Government Accountability Office warned that leasing space in foreign-owned buildings "could present security risks such as espionage and unauthorized cyber and physical access.” The UK’s National Security and Investment Act took effect in January 2022, but real estate was not among the sensitive sectors subject to its mandatory screening requirements for acquisitions. Read responses Responses Chen Hongtian/Cheung Kei group: The Cheung Kei group didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In statement posted on its website in 2023 the group said that “like all heavy asset holders”, it was “experiencing a phase of cash problems” and that its “overall asset scale and asset quality” were “very high, with a low debt ratio among peers.” At the time the group was “selling some equity in some assets and actively negotiating repayment arrangements with relevant financial institutions” and said it “believed that subsequent financial institution issues will be properly resolved.” ICBC London: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Jovial Link Holdings Ltd. for 5 Churchill Place; Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., Cheung Kwan Holdings Ltd. for 20 Canada Square (London properties) Start dates of loans 2022 Amount $61.7M / $143.5MTotal loan commitments From the China Capital files In their own words: About 5 Churchill Place, from a credit loan application: The deal as outlined herein offers ICBC London an ideal opportunity to assist an incoming Chinese client in the purchase of a major “trophy” asset that is both well let to tenants of significant covenant strengths and well located within the popular Canary Wharf developmentRisk Trapping In Debt 05 ICBC records on Zambia show a lender watching a borrower facing growing financial risks, while quietly putting protections in place for its own loans. ICBC financed a range of major projects in the country, providing loans for government-owned housing, a hospital, an airport and power projects running to hundreds of millions of dollars. Among them was a $285 million loan approved in 2010 to ZESCO, Zambia's state-owned power company, for two power transmission projects. Between 2015 and 2018, ICBC provided or participated in at least six more loans to ZESCO, totaling $1.2 billion according to AidData estimates, even as the bank was aware of mounting financial pressures on both Zambia and ZESCO. By 2017, a sovereign risk assessment in the bank's files described Zambia as facing limited financing options, rising interest costs, and substantial debt—and specifically pointed to financial pressures on ZESCO. Government net debt had climbed from 23% of GDP in 2013 to an estimated 57% in 2017, while debt costs consumed nearly a quarter of government revenue. ICBC had classified ZESCO as a high-risk client since 2018, citing Zambia's country risk, politically exposed persons and historical adverse media coverage including bribery and corruption allegations, according to a 2023 internal report. Despite these concerns, the bank continued its lending relationship with ZESCO, requiring annual reviews. ICBC built protections into its lending. ZESCO maintained a debt-service reserve account at ICBC London for repayments on the $285 million loan. Money deposited into the account could only be withdrawn by ICBC's head office, which was also the lender, agent and security trustee. ZESCO’s financial precarity triggered a cascade of credit problems. By March 2020, its failure to pay Maamba Collieries Ltd., a Zambian power supplier, had left Maamba unable to meet its own loan obligations to ICBC and other lenders. ICBC records show that lenders sent letters to Zambia's Ministry of Finance seeking government support, contacted Chinese state-owned insurer Sinosure and discussed restructuring the loan. ICBC officials warned that Maamba's loan would be classified as non-performing if payments remained overdue for more than 90 days. The documents offer a window into how the bank continued banking a financially strained borrower while using safeguards to limit its own losses. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. title: Europe and China 1 – The Arrival of the People’s Republic
zh_title: 欧洲与中国 1 – 中华人民共和国的到来
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: 这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词的出现，世界已经站在了门口。

这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济正在快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词成为每次企业峰会的议程，世界已经来到了门口。为了重现这一转变，历史学家必须首先确定其背后的政治人物。即使天安门上的鲜血被冲洗干净——当未来的国家主席习近平的妻子、歌手彭丽媛为戒严部队唱小夜曲时——许多中国领导人知道他们犯了一个可怕的错误。其中包括习近平的父亲、两次被清洗的退伍军人习仲勋，他公开赞扬镇压“反革命暴乱”的“明智”和“坚决”决定，但私下里对经济改革的挫折表示哀悼。习仲勋亲自执掌南方经济强国广东，在20世纪80年代把它变成了吸引外资的世界工厂。他是影响 1989 年后中国下一届领导人选择的造王者之一。
这两名新面孔是从沿海贸易大都市上海走上来的。江泽民是上海共产党的领导人，也是一名受过苏联训练的工程师，后来成为国家主席和党的领导人。然而，关键人物却是一位名叫朱镕基的市长，他是一位出生于1928年、头脑敏锐的技术官僚。他先后担任央行行长和总理。天安门事件发生时，两人曾监督和平结束中国商业首都的大规模抗议活动。上海没有发生大屠杀。相反，朱在电视上发出严厉警告，当局则部署警察和民兵慢慢平息示威活动。上海很快就恢复了商业秩序。欧洲公司是浦东新金融区的第一批投资者。两位领导人不顾党内左派的强烈反对，决心让中国向世界经济开放。他们的活动可以通过日内瓦世贸组织的档案来追踪，这是谈判的宝贵指南。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the first of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. In the 1990s, the shadow of Tiananmen Square fell across Europe’s trade relations with China. The massacre of protesters in 1989 marked a return to dictatorship and wiped out hopes of political reform. European firms drew back, an arms embargo was imposed, and political pressure grew to isolate “the butchers of Beijing.” Yet by the end of the decade China had swept triumphantly into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), its economy was growing fast, and the world was at its door as a new word, “globalization,” set the agenda at every corporate summit. To reconstruct the turnaround, a historian must first identify the political personalities behind it. Even as the blood was hosed off Tiananmen — and while the future President Xi Jinping’s wife, the singer Peng Liyuan, serenaded the martial law troops — many Chinese leaders knew they had made a terrible blunder. They included Xi Jinping’s father, the twice-purged army veteran Xi Zhongxun, who paid homage in public to the “wise” and “resolute” decision to suppress “a counter-revolutionary riot” but in private mourned the setback to economic reform. Xi Zhongxun himself had taken charge of the southern powerhouse of Guangdong, turning it into a workshop for the world that drew in foreign investment through the 1980s. He was one of the kingmakers who influenced the choice of China’s next leaders after 1989. The new faces were two men who had stepped up from the coastal trading metropolis of Shanghai. Jiang Zemin, the Communist Party boss in Shanghai, a Soviet-trained engineer, became President and leader of the party. Yet the key figure turned out to be a dynamo called Zhu Rongji, the city’s mayor, a sharp-witted technocrat born in 1928. In succession, he became governor of the central bank and prime minister. The duo had overseen a peaceful end to mass protests in China’s commercial capital at the time of Tiananmen. There was no massacre in Shanghai. Instead, Zhu went on television to issue a grim warning, and the authorities deployed police and militia to quieten the demonstrations slowly. Shanghai was soon back in business. European companies were in the first wave of investors in the city’s new financial district of Pudong. Both leaders were determined to open China up to the world economy, defying vocal opposition from leftists in the party. Their campaign can be traced through the archives of the WTO in Geneva, an invaluable guide to the negotiations. Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. As early as 1986, China had applied to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), but the major trading powers had decided to transform the GATT into a new body that would govern services as well as trade from January 1, 1995. It was too soon for China to join the new World Trade Organization at its birth, but negotiations began in earnest. The EU formed a negotiating bloc in rounds of bilateral talks between China and all its partners, which the WTO would then orchestrate into a package. Accession was vital to China, as Zhu Rongji argued in party councils. In 1993, for example, the People’s Republic recorded a trade deficit of more than $12bn, due to the cost of imports for modernization. At the same time, China’s foreign trade had soared to $195bn from $20bn in 1978, the start of the “reform and open up” era. John Bond, the chairman of HSBC Holdings, heard Zhu speak and realized that the Communist cadre had posed a modern version of the famous “Needham Question” raised by the Cambridge polymath, Joseph Needham, of why modern science had enjoyed a meteoric rise in Europe but not in China. “How can 22% of the world’s population account for less than 4% of the world’s GNP?” Bond asked. The WTO documents show the intricacy and the scale of that challenge. The rewards were obvious. In the five years after 1990, Guangdong Province, the former fiefdom of Xi Jinping’s father, saw an expansion across key industries of 40% every 12 months, according to the official Statistical Yearbook for 1996. Formidable obstacles remained. Zhu Rongji fought battles in Beijing to push through a 1994 package of changes to banking, finance, taxation, investment, foreign exchange and foreign trade. The working party in Geneva met behind closed doors 21 times between March 1996 and September 2001. The Europeans pressed hard on intellectual property, copyright protection, patents, trademarks (matters of great concern to Germany), test data, trade secrets, government procurement, minority shareholder rights, and judicial remedies. The WTO working party report alone ran to almost 200 pages. In the end, Europe had a deal. The fate of China was put into American hands. Between September and December 2001, the Clinton administration waged cliff-edge negotiations with the Chinese that remain controversial to this day. A myth has grown that China was ushered into the WTO by vested interests pushing a globalization and free trade agenda. The record shows that China’s road to accession was, in fact, long, painstaking and hard-fought. The final agreement imposed harsher conditions on China than any other nation when its membership became formal on December 11, 2001. It ran to 1,500 pages and weighed 13 kg (29 lbs.). Zhu Rongji saw his country become the world’s second largest economy, the biggest exporter, and the world’s largest holder of foreign currency reserves. He died earlier this year. “It was win-win,’ said the Hong Kong representative in Geneva from 1994 to 2002, Stuart Harbinson. “That was the conventional wisdom.” Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese. content:
特朗普表示他和习近平希望制定温和的人工智能规则中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 20 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
特朗普表示他和习近平希望制定温和的人工智能规则
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示，他和中国国家主席习近平都希望制定合理的人工智能安全法规，并将共同制定规则。特朗普补充说，他在深圳会议期间没有详细讨论英伟达或首席执行官黄仁勋涉嫌的间谍关系
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周四在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示，他和中国国家主席习近平都希望出于安全目的对人工智能进行监管，并将共同制定合理的人工智能规则。
特朗普还表示，本周特朗普在深圳会见中国国家主席期间，他没有与习近平过多谈论英伟达或其首席执行官黄仁勋与一名所谓的中国间谍的关系。
中国驻华盛顿大使馆周四在一份声明中表示，两国应“加强沟通协调，防范人工智能安全风险，确保人工智能始终处于人类掌控之下。”
美国和中国正在竞相建立卓越的人工智能模型，两国都认为这对于军事和技术领先地位具有战略重要性。两位领导人在那场比赛的一个复杂时刻会面。 《纽约时报》十月份报道称，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被指控为北京从事间谍活动的女子有过恋爱关系。路透社尚未独立证实该女子是间谍。
英伟达是全球领先的先进芯片制造商，这些芯片广泛用于开发尖端人工智能模型。美国多年来一直寻求限制中国获得英伟达芯片，因为它不希望中国军方从中受益。

Trump says he and Xi want moderate AI rules | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 20 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Trump says he and Xi want moderate AI rules
US President Donald Trump said in a Fox News interview that he and Chinese President Xi Jinping both want reasonable AI regulations for safety and will work together on the rules. Trump added he did not discuss Nvidia or CEO Jensen Huang's alleged spy relationship at length during their Shenzhen mee
US President Donald Trump said in an interview with Fox News on Thursday that he and Chinese President Xi Jinping both want artificial-intelligence regulations for safety purposes and will work together on reasonable AI rules.
Trump also said he did not talk too much with Xi about Nvidia or its CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy during Trump's visit with the Chinese president this week in Shenzhen.
The Chinese embassy in Washington said in a statement on Thursday that the two countries should “strengthen communication and coordination, prevent the security risks of AI and ensure that AI is always under human control.”
The US and China are racing to build superior AI models, which both countries view as strategically important for military and technological leadership. The leaders met at a complicated time in that race. The New York Times reported in October that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a woman accused of spying for Beijing. Reuters has not independently confirmed that the woman is a spy.
Nvidia is the world's leading maker of the advanced chips that are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models. The US has sought for years to limit China's access to Nvidia's chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

title: Asia’s stock markets dive as Anthropic debut fails to allay AI bubble fears
zh_title: Anthropic 首次亮相未能缓解人工智能泡沫担忧，亚洲股市暴跌
source: 菲律宾在中国紧张局势中加强其最北端的防御
summary: Anthropic 首次亮相未能缓解人工智能泡沫担忧，亚洲股市暴跌金融市场新闻|半岛电视台分享 Anthropic 首次亮相未能缓解社交媒体上对人工智能泡沫的担忧，亚洲股市暴跌一名人走在日本东京的东京证券交易所前 [文件：Eugene Hoshiko/美联社照片] 尽管 Anthropic 首次亮相，但由于对人工智能繁荣不可持续的担忧继续打压市场情绪，亚洲股市开盘大幅下跌。由于投资者对克劳德创作者的兴奋，日本、韩国、台湾和香港市场周五大幅下跌
content:
Anthropic 首次亮相未能缓解人工智能泡沫担忧，亚洲股市暴跌金融市场新闻|半岛电视台
Anthropic 的首次亮相未能缓解社交媒体上对人工智能泡沫的担忧，亚洲股市暴跌
一个人走在日本东京的东京证券交易所前[文件：Eugene Hoshiko/美联社照片]
尽管 Anthropic 首次亮相，但由于对人工智能繁荣不可持续的担忧继续打压市场情绪，亚洲股市开盘大幅下跌。
周五，日本、韩国、台湾和香港市场大幅下跌，投资者对克劳德创始人公开上市的兴奋情绪未能缓解人们对支撑人工智能的数万亿美元投资可持续性的担忧。
list 1 of 4 海地警方称 34 名帮派成员在首都突袭中丧生
list 2 of 4“完全搞砸了一切”：马拉维的燃料危机导致混乱
4 名民主党人中的名单 3 称律师事务所向特朗普政府提供了 1,180 万美元的免费服务
list 4 of 4Meta 重新思考 2030 年气候目标，因为人工智能数据中心导致排放增加
东京基准日经 225 指数下跌 4.8%，首尔综合指数下跌超过 5%。
台北股市下跌 6.4%，香港恒生指数下跌 2%。
法国兴业银行亚洲股票策略师 Rajat Agarwal 表示，抛售反映了人们对人工智能主导的增长正在放缓以及“增长峰值阶段”可能已经过去的担忧。
“第二个因素是我们所看到的需求真空，”阿加瓦尔告诉半岛电视台。
“在外国人不买房的时候，国内投资者还能坚持多久还有待观察，特别是在韩国，其回撤更为严重。”
与华尔街一样，亚洲主要交易所也严重受到人工智能的影响。
该地区是全球人工智能生态系统中一些关键参与者的所在地，包括韩国存储芯片制造商 SK 海力士和三星电子、台湾合约芯片制造商台积电和日本投资控股公司软银集团。
近年来，科技公司在人工智能领域投入了数万亿美元，期望未来能获得巨额利润，并引发了人们对债务引发的市场泡沫的担忧，让人想起 2000 年互联网泡沫破裂之前的挥霍行为。
根据技术洞察公司 Gartner 的数据，全球人工智能相关投资预计到 2026 年将达到 2.7 万亿美元，2027 年将达到 3.6 万亿美元。
香港 Union Bancaire Privee 亚洲高级经济学家卡洛斯·卡萨诺瓦 (Carlos Casanova) 表示，多个市场的抛售反映了“对人工智能投资理论的信心崩溃”。
卡萨诺瓦告诉半岛电视台：“全球科技股本周有所回落，其中以芯片为主的亚洲市场首当其冲。”
他表示：“Anthropic 的重磅 IPO 几乎没有缓解人们对人工智能相关股票前景的更广泛担忧，而且可能使这场辩论具体化。”
他补充道：“随着投资者转向新发行的股票，上市似乎并没有提升更广泛的人工智能综合体，而是转移了现有人工智能领域的流动性。”
“英伟达本周早些时候的财报也未能给市场带来所寻求的保证。”
由于有传言称英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋与中国情报人员或资产有染，华盛顿采取行动打压中国获取先进芯片，这也打压了市场情绪。

【原文 English Original】
Asia’s stock markets dive as Anthropic debut fails to allay AI bubble fears | Financial Markets News | Al Jazeera
Share Asia’s stock markets dive as Anthropic debut fails to allay AI bubble fears on social media
A person walks in front of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in Tokyo, Japan [File: Eugene Hoshiko/AP Photo]
Asian stock markets have opened with steep losses as fears that the AI boom is unsustainable continue to weigh on sentiment despite Anthropic’s blockbuster debut.
Markets in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong fell sharply on Friday, as investor excitement around the Claude creator’s public listing failed to allay concerns about the sustainability of the multi-trillion-dollar investments propping up AI.

list 2 of 4‘Completely messed up everything’: Malawi’s fuel crisis causes chaos
list 3 of 4Democrats say law firm gave $11.8m in free services to Trump administration
list 4 of 4Meta rethinks 2030 climate goals as AI data centres drive emissions up
Tokyo’s benchmark Nikkei 225 tumbled as much as 4.8 percent, while Seoul’s Kospi fell more than 5 percent.
In Taipei, the Taiex plunged 6.4 percent, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index dipped as much as 2 percent.
The sell-off reflects concerns that AI-led growth is slowing down and the “peak growth phase” may have passed, said Rajat Agarwal, an Asia equity strategist with Societe Generale.
“The second element is on the demand vacuum that we are seeing,” Agarwal told Al Jazeera.
“At the time when foreigners are not buying, it is to be seen how long can the domestic investors stay put, particularly in Korea, on which the drawdown has been more severe.”
Like Wall Street, Asia’s main bourses are heavily exposed to AI.
The region is home to some of the key players in the global AI ecosystem, including South Korean memory chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, Taiwanese contract chipmaker TSMC, and Japanese investment holding company SoftBank Group.
Tech firms have poured trillions of dollars into AI in recent years, expecting huge future profits and stoking fears of a debt-fuelled market bubble reminiscent of the splurge that preceded the 2000 dot-com crash.
Global AI-related investment is projected to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.
Carlos Casanova, senior economist for Asia at Union Bancaire Privee in Hong Kong, said the sell-off in multiple markets reflected a “collapse in confidence in the AI investment thesis”.
“Global technology stocks have retreated throughout the week, with Asia’s chip-heavy markets bearing the brunt of the sell-off,” Casanova told Al Jazeera.
“Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO did little to ease broader concerns about the outlook for AI-related equities and may, if anything, have crystallised the debate,” he said.
“Rather than lifting the broader AI complex, the listing appears to have diverted liquidity from established AI plays as investors rotated into the new issue,” he added.
“Nvidia’s earnings earlier this week also failed to provide the reassurance markets were seeking.”
Market sentiment has also been dampened by moves in Washington to clamp down on China’s access to advanced chips amid claims that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was romantically involved with a Chinese intelligence operative or asset.
The US Bureau of Industry and Security this week announced new export licence requirements aimed at preventing Chinese AI developers from remotely accessing top-of-the-line computing power at data centres in third countries, mainly in Southeast Asia.
In the latest in a series of probes facing Nvidia, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday that his office had served a subpoena on the chip giant seeking information about whether its advanced chips made their way to China and whether it misled investors.
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment about the probe.
The market retreat in Asia followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, even as Anthropic shares jumped 17 percent on their first day of trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York.
Anthropic’s stock price opened at $111.50 before settling just above $97, vaulting the Claude creator into the ranks of the world’s most valuable companies.
The San Francisco-based AI giant’s market debut came after it raised $81.3bn in the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history, leapfrogging the $75bn SpaceX initially raised in June.
Despite the excitement around Anthropic, key indexes closed in the red, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite down 2.3 percent and the broader S&P 500 dropping 2 percent.

title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
zh_title: 以社区为中心的学术界为科罗拉多州农民带来人工智能工具
summary: 科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”东 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县扩建项目 Tit
content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

summary: VMware 修补了自 9 月份以来遭受攻击的 vCenter 零日漏洞 VMware 修补了自 9 月份以来遭受攻击的 vCenter 零日漏洞 VMware 修补了自 9 月份以来遭受攻击的 vCenter 零日漏洞 Broadcom 发布了安全更新，以修复一个重要的 VMware vCenter Server 身份验证绕过漏洞，该漏洞被中国黑客自 2026 年 9 月以来在零日攻击中利用。该漏洞的编号为 CVE-2026-123890，影响 vCenter Server 中的 VMware Directory Service，vCenter Server 是组织用来管理 VMware 虚拟化环境的管理平台。雅阁
content:
VMware 修补了自 9 月份以来遭受攻击的 vCenter 零日漏洞
VMware 修补了自 9 月份以来遭受攻击的 vCenter 零日漏洞
VMware 修补了自 9 月份以来遭受攻击的 vCenter 零日漏洞
Broadcom 发布了安全更新，以修复一个关键的 VMware vCenter Server 身份验证绕过漏洞，自 2026 年 9 月以来，与中国有关的黑客在零日攻击中利用了该漏洞。
该漏洞编号为 CVE-2026-123890，影响 vCenter Server 中的 VMware Directory Service，vCenter Server 是组织用来管理 VMware 虚拟化环境的管理平台。
据 Broadcom 称，该漏洞允许未经身份验证的攻击者通过网络访问易受攻击的 vCenter Server，从而绕过身份验证并获得未经授权的访问。
成功利用该漏洞可以让攻击者获得 vCenter 的管理访问权限，从而控制服务器管理的虚拟机。
Broadcom 于 11 月 19 日在 VMSA-2026-0009 中修补了该漏洞，同时还修复了影响 VMware SDDC Manager 和 VMware Tools for Windows 的其他四个漏洞。
Broadcom 的安全公告中写道：“如果您运行的任何版本的 VMware vCenter、SDDC Manager 或 VMware Tools for Windows 早于 VMSA 中列为“已修复”的版本，您就会受到影响。”
“这包括独立部署的 vCenter 和 SDDC Manager，以及作为 VMware Cloud Foundation、VMware vSphere Foundation、VMware Telco Cloud Platform 和 VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure 的一部分，以及安装在 Windows 虚拟机中的 VMware Tools。”
该公司将vCenter漏洞视为紧急更新，敦促组织尽快安装补丁。
博通表示，尽管网络限制和防火墙控制可以帮助减少漏洞，但目前还没有针对这些漏洞的官方解决方法。
此外，无论是否启用增强型链接模式，该漏洞都会影响 vCenter。
虽然 Broadcom 尚未确认该漏洞已被利用，但 Google Mandiant 的研究人员已记录了利用 CVE-2026-123890 的攻击。
中国黑客利用VMware零日漏洞
在今天发布的一份报告中，Mandiant 和谷歌威胁情报组织 (GTIG) 透露，一个被追踪为 Armoury Castle（以前称为 UNC5221）的疑似中国国家支持的黑客组织于 2026 年 9 月上旬利用了 CVE-2026-123890。
Mandiant 解释道：“成功利用该漏洞会导致远程身份验证绕过，从而创建一个以administrator@vsphere.local 身份建立的经过身份验证的会话。”
“使用经过身份验证的管理员会话，攻击者可以利用 vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC 接口 vmdirdbcp 执行任意命令并获取文件，包括 data.mdb 数据库。”
Armory Castle 是一个网络间谍组织，以利用企业网络设备（包括 Citrix NetScaler 和 Ivanti Connect Secure 设备）中的零日漏洞来破坏企业网络并部署自定义恶意软件而闻名。
该组织最近还与利用 BeyondTrust Remote Support 零日漏洞的攻击有关，编号为 CVE-2026-102764，该漏洞自 8 月底以来一直被利用。
Mandiant 表示，VMware 漏洞是同一入侵活动的一部分，攻击者首先入侵 BeyondTrust Remote Support 设备，然后横向进入内部 Linux 系统并针对 VMware 基础设施。

【原文 English Original】
VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
Broadcom has released security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server, a management platform organizations use to manage VMware virtualized environments.
According Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a vulnerable vCenter Server to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.
Successful exploitation can allow attackers to obtain administrative access to vCenter, giving them control over the virtual machines managed by the server.
Broadcom patched the vulnerability on November 19 in VMSA-2026-0009, which also fixes four other vulnerabilities affecting VMware SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows.
"You are affected if you are running any version of VMware vCenter, SDDC Manager, or VMware Tools for Windows prior to the versions listed as "fixed" in the VMSA," Broadcom's security advisory reads.
"This includes vCenter and SDDC Manager deployed standalone and as part of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Telco Cloud Platform, and VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure, as well as VMware Tools installed in Windows virtual machines."
The company considers the vCenter vulnerability as an emergency update, urging organizations to install the patches as soon as possible.
Broadcom says there are no official workarounds for the vulnerabilities, although network restrictions and firewall controls can help reduce exposure.
Furthermore, the vulnerability affects vCenter regardless of whether Enhanced Linked Mode is enabled.
While Broadcom has not confirmed that the flaw was exploited, researchers at Google's Mandiant have documented attacks exploiting CVE-2026-123890.
Chinese hackers exploited VMware zero-day
In a report published today, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) revealed that a suspected Chinese state-sponsored hacking group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-123890 in early September 2026.
"Successful exploitation results in a remote authentication bypass which creates an authenticated session established as administrator@vsphere.local," explains Mandiant.
"Using the authenticated administrator session, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands and acquire files, including the data.mdb database, by leveraging the vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC interface vmdirdbcp."
Armory Castle is a cyberespionage group known for exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in enterprise network appliances, including Citrix NetScaler and Ivanti Connect Secure devices, to breach corporate networks and deploy custom malware.
The group was also recently linked to attacks exploiting a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-102764, which has been exploited since late August.
Mandiant says the VMware exploitation was part of the same intrusion campaign, with the attackers first compromising BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances before moving laterally into internal Linux systems and targeting VMware infrastructure.
After gaining access to an internal Linux appliance, the hackers deployed the "SLIMSAVAGE" web shells to maintain persistent access, escalated privileges to root, and scanned the internal network for VMware systems.
SLIMSAVAGE webshell deployed on Linux servers
The attackers then used a custom Golang exploitation tool named BONESAW to exploit CVE-2026-123890 and compromise a VMware vCenter Server.
Mandiant observed the tool successfully creating a vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO) administrator account and stealing the server's directory database, which can be used to extract further credentials.
BONESAW can also extract SAML signing keys, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens and gain administrative access to VMware environments.
Following the exploitation, the hackers deployed another tool called SAWSNAKE, which enables so-called Golden SAML attacks to forge authentication tokens, bypass multifactor authentication, and impersonate legitimate users.
During the attack, the attackers also deployed additional web shells and backdoors, including CAGEMATCH, BEARBONES, and LAZYBONES, to execute commands, transfer files, steal credentials, and maintain access to compromised systems.
The attacks ultimately allowed Armory Castle to move deeper into the victims' virtualized environments, access ESXi hosts, and extract sensitive information from virtual machines, including Windows Active Directory database files.
Mandiant says the use of two zero-day vulnerabilities in the same campaign, along with multiple malware families tailored to the targeted platforms, demonstrates the threat actor's technical expertise.
The researchers urge admins to apply the VMware security updates as soon as possible and configure additional security controls to protect their virtualization infrastructure against future attacks.

title: China, US, Russia issue ‘Declaration toward Peace’ after first summit
zh_title: 中美俄首次峰会后发表《和平宣言》
summary: 中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人举行史无前例的峰会后于周四发表了《和平宣言》，提出了改革联合国和控制国际刑事法院的共同目标。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达麒麟山庄参加三方会议时合影留念。照片：Vyacheslav Prokofyev/法新社。习近平、唐纳德·特鲁
content:
中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人举行史无前例的峰会后于周四发表了《和平宣言》，提出了改革联合国和控制国际刑事法院的共同目标。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达麒麟山庄参加三方会议时合影留念。照片：Vyacheslav Prokofyev/法新社。习近平、特朗普和普京在中国会晤的背景复杂，俄罗斯在乌克兰的攻势持续多年，特朗普在中东陷入困境，而崛起的中国则希望加强在东亚的影响力。白宫版本的声明称，“三位国家元首就当前国际形势深入交换了意见，致力于维护战略稳定和国际安全。” “我们讨论了民主问题。什么是民主？它是什么？这是某些圈子联合起来的自由秩序，现在仍在试图强加给全世界，”普京在南方城市深圳举行的新闻发布会上说。三人围坐在一张深色的大圆桌前，围绕从核武器到乌克兰战争等重大话题发表了开场白，圆桌中央摆放着粉红色的花朵。
麒麟山庄的闭门讨论在一个小时二十分钟后结束。特朗普称领导人正在“创造历史”，普京则称他们写下了“外交史上新的一页”。习近平表示，“三个国家在维护世界和平方面有着共同的观点”。在返回华盛顿的途中，特朗普召集了一次欧洲领导人会议，讨论乌克兰问题并向他们通报三方峰会的最新情况。 2026 年 2 月，布鲁塞尔欧盟委员会总部前悬挂着乌克兰和欧盟旗帜。照片：欧盟委员会。并非所有欧洲领导人都对此印象深刻：德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨称特朗普-习近平-普京会谈是一次“合影”，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙表示，这不会“导致世界重组”。特朗普表示，他将于周五举行新闻发布会，介绍他的“伟大且具有重大意义的中国之行”。国际刑事法院、联合国和石油在联合声明中，特朗普、习近平和普京“认识到国家同意和尊重国家官员豁免权的原则至关重要，并同意国际刑事法院和其他类似机构不得滥用管辖权”。普京受到国际刑事法院逮捕令的制裁，而特朗普政府则誓言要“一砖一瓦”解散该法院。国际刑事法院。资料照片：维基共享资源。
领导人表示，他们“致力于改革联合国，使联合国能够更有效地应对全球挑战，履行其国际和平与安全的基本使命”。联合声明称，各国计划增加成品油供应和生产，并重申“稳定能源流动”的重要性。这次峰会引发了人们的担忧，担心这三人想要将全球划分为势力范围，例如通过做出影响乌克兰而不是基辅或欧洲的决定。但特朗普表示，他希望“欧洲站在他一边”就乌克兰问题达成协议

【原文 English Original】
China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court in check. Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump pose for photos as they arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP. Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China against a complex backdrop, with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, Trump bogged down in the Middle East and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security,” a White House version of the statement said. “We discussed the question of democracy. And what is democracy? It’s what? It’s the liberal order that certain circles put together and still now are trying to impose on the whole world,” Putin told a news conference in the southern city of Shenzhen. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the leaders were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. On his way home to Washington, Trump called into a meeting of European leaders to discuss Ukraine and update them on his three-way summit. Ukrainian and European Union flags in front of the European Commission headquarters in Brussels in February 2026. Photo: European Commission. Not all of those European leaders were impressed: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the Trump-Xi-Putin talks a “photo op”, and French President Emmanuel Macron said it would not “lead to a reorganisation of the world”. Trump said he would give a press conference on Friday about his “Great and Highly Consequential Trip” to China. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, Trump, Xi and Putin “recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant, while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. International Criminal Court. File photo: Wikicommons. The leaders said they were “committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security”. The joint statement said the countries plan to boost supply and production of refined petroleum products, and reaffirmed the importance of “stable energy flows”. The summit stoked fears that the three men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence , for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. But Trump said he wanted to make a deal on Ukraine “with Europe by his side”, accourding to special US envoy Jared Kushner. ‘Reducing nuclear risks’ Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”. Putin responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — their third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting a “very special relationship”. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Beijing, Washington and Moscow previously gave different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a forum of 21 economies around the Pacific Rim. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. China’s nuclear arsenal. File Photo: CCTV screenshot. The final statement said that the countries would “conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.” ‘Cheap violin’ Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi met Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and a flyover. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions”, said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said.

zh_title: 香港贸易办事处在华盛顿推广商机
summary: 香港贸易办事处在华盛顿推广商机 |中国劳工布告栏 周五, 20 11 月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港贸易办事处在华盛顿宣传商机 香港贸易办事处在华盛顿宣传该市的商机，强调其作为“超级联络人”的作用以及为美国公司提供机会的北领地的发展。香港驻华盛顿经济贸易办事处处长陆子在活动中推广香港的商机
content:
香港贸易办事处在华盛顿推广商机 |中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 20 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港贸易办事处在华盛顿推广商机
香港驻华盛顿贸易办事处宣传香港的商机，强调其作为“超级联系人”的作用以及为美国公司提供机会的北部地区的发展。
香港驻华盛顿经济贸易办事处在一次活动中宣传香港的商机，处长陆子贤强调香港作为“超级联系人”的角色。她于2026年11月20日致辞时表示，香港一直连接各地人才、企业和市场，为国际企业开拓中国内地及亚太市场提供策略平台。
陆克文概述了《施政报告》和香港第一个五年规划的要点，强调香港致力于长期经济发展、加强国际联系和深化贸易合作。她指出香港在金融服务、贸易、航运和航空方面的传统优势，同时积极推动创新和科技发展。
她说，通过巩固“四中心一高地”地位，香港旨在增强国际竞争力，开辟新的投资和贸易机会。陆先生还介绍了法律和争议解决服务方面的机遇，包括努力使香港成为国际调解和仲裁中心。
陆先生重点介绍了香港最大的发展项目——北领地，该项目占地约占全市土地总面积的三分之一。该项目旨在利用毗邻大湾区供应链和创新生态系统的优势，促进教育、技术、研究和人才之间的协同效应。
“北领地的发展为美国企业带来了巨大机遇。美国公司在许多关键领域拥有世界一流的专业知识，对于该项目的发展至关重要。我们欢迎美国企业参与并探索进一步的合作机会。”
在复杂的全球商业环境中，香港保持开放。 “我们希望向美国公司发出一个明确的信息——香港是建立联系、投资和扩张的理想场所。我们始终欢迎美国企业参与香港的发展。”
投资促进局纽约办事处主任谢毅随后介绍了香港发展带来的商机，以及该局如何为希望在香港设立或扩张的美国企业提供定制服务。

Hong Kong trade office promotes business opportunities in Washington | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 20 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong trade office promotes business opportunities in Washington
Hong Kong's trade office in Washington has promoted the city's business opportunities, highlighting its role as a 'super connector' and the development of the Northern Territories, which offers opportunities for US firms.
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Washington has promoted the city's business opportunities at an event where director Luk Tsz-yin emphasised Hong Kong's role as a 'super connector'. Speaking on 20 November 2026, she said Hong Kong has been linking talent, enterprises and markets from different places, providing a strategic platform for international firms to explore the Chinese mainland and Asia-Pacific markets.
Luk outlined key points from the Policy Address and Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, stressing the city's commitment to long-term economic development, strengthening international ties and deepening trade cooperation. She noted Hong Kong's traditional strengths in financial services, trade, shipping and aviation, while actively promoting innovation and technology development.
By reinforcing its status as 'four centres and one highland', Hong Kong aims to enhance its international competitiveness and open up new investment and trade opportunities, she said. Luk also introduced opportunities in legal and dispute resolution services, including efforts to make Hong Kong a hub for international mediation and arbitration.
Luk highlighted the Northern Territories, Hong Kong's largest development project, which covers about one-third of the city's total land area. The project aims to promote synergy among education, technology, research and talent, leveraging the proximity to the Greater Bay Area's supply chain and innovation ecosystem.
'The development of the Northern Territories brings huge opportunities for US firms. US companies have world-class expertise in many key areas and are crucial to the project's development. We welcome US firms to participate and explore further cooperation opportunities,' Luk said.
Amid a complex global business environment, Hong Kong remains open. 'We want to send a clear message to US firms — Hong Kong is an ideal place to build connections, invest and expand. We always welcome US firms to participate in Hong Kong's development,' she added.
Investment Promotion Agency's New York office director Xie Yi later introduced the business opportunities arising from Hong Kong's developments and how the agency provides customised services for US firms looking to set up or expand in Hong Kong.

一公斤氧化钇 (Y2O3) 在中国的价格约为 9 美元，但在欧洲约为 1,150 美元，是后者的 125 倍多。在北京收紧稀土出口管制之前（在新窗口中打开），价格差距不大。现在，日本首当其冲受到供应紧张的影响。钇用于电子和激光等高科技制造以及癌症治疗。
东京将价格差异描述为一个全球性问题。日本经济产业省（METI）官员表示，中国的钇出口已陷入停滞，导致全球价格走高。
但贸易数据讲述了一个更尖锐的故事。据报道，2026 年前 9 个月，中国对日本的氧化钇出口量骤降 98%（在新窗口中打开），从 887 吨降至仅 18 吨。中国的全球出口仅下降了26%，而对日本以外目的地的出口量却增加了一倍多。这种差异表明有选择性的供应限制。
日本制造商正在争先恐后地寻找替代供应。东京（在新窗口中打开）还就钇短缺问题向华盛顿和其他盟友寻求帮助。
时机很重要。中国于 2025 年 4 月对包括钇在内的几种中重稀土实行出口许可。但在日本首相高市早苗于 2025 年 11 月暗示中国对台湾的军事封锁可能构成威胁生存的局势 — — 在某些条件下允许集体自卫的法律门槛后，紧张局势升级。
北京方面认为这些言论跨越了红线。据报道，在中国于 2026 年 1 月限制向日本军事用户和军事相关最终用途的军民两用出口 (在新窗口中打开) 之前，对日本的钇出货量较 12 月有所减少。2 月，北京禁止向 20 个日本实体 (在新窗口中打开) 出口，并对另外 20 个实体进行了严格审查。
一种鲜为人知的稀土已成为不太可能的地缘政治杠杆来源。
小要素，大杠杆
尽管钇的原子量相对较轻，但在商业上与重稀土归为一类。与用于高性能永磁体的钕和镝不同，钇的价值在于先进陶瓷和特种涂层。钇稳定氧化锆可保护喷气发动机部件免受极端高温的影响，而钇基化合物可保护半导体设备免受腐蚀性等离子体的影响。它还用于激光器、光学材料和医疗器械。
制造商需要的数量相对较少，但短缺可能会扰乱价值数百万美元设备的生产。航空航天和航空航天领域合格的替代材料
