US lawmakers in Washington are closing in on a deal to ban Chinese cars from the US, according to people familiar with the matter.
For now, both presidents want to reinforce their personal ties ahead of a potentially more confrontational period when the new US Congress takes office in January, said William Yang, senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group.
“The Democrats are signalling strongly they are going to look hard into pushing the administration to enforce or reinstate strict export control measures against high-end AI semiconductor chips,” he said. “Beijing is sensing there might be a storm coming in the next few weeks.” BLOOMBERG

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，一名助手向中国官员提出了两名美国人被北京拘留的案件。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 20 日 06:25
更新于 2026 年 11 月 20 日 12:30
特朗普表示，一名助手在与习近平的深圳峰会上向中国官员提出了美国人陈友林和敏津被拘留的问题。
陈自 2024 年 11 月以来一直被关押，并被指控从事间谍活动；辛于六月前往云南参加学术会议后被捕。
他们的案件很重要，因为华盛顿称他们“被错误拘留”，而中国则表示根据自己的法律处理此类案件。
华盛顿 - 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普 11 月 19 日告诉路透社，一名助手在访问中国期间向中国官员提出了两名美国人陈友林和敏津的案件，他们被美国认定为被北京错误拘留。
特朗普在与中国和俄罗斯外长举行的深圳峰会飞回华盛顿时与路透社通了电话。
陈是一位出生于中国的地震学家，擅长探测朝鲜核试验，自 2024 年 11 月以来一直被中国关押；缅甸问题研究员辛于六月访问中国西南部期间被捕。
国务卿马可·卢比奥将这两人认定为错误拘留，这使得释放他们成为美国的首要任务。中国不承认这一指定，并表示拘留案件是根据中国法律处理的。
11 月 18 日，共和党议员敦促特朗普向习近平施压，释放两人。但特朗普告诉路透社，一名助手已向中方提出了他们的案件。
他说，这些人是被中国关押的“少数”美国人之一。
特朗普继续说道：“我们已经把很多人从很多国家释放了。”他指的是自 2025 年 1 月开始他的第二个任期以来，其他政府释放了美国人。
“你知道我从白俄罗斯和其他地方运出了数百个。”
据美国官员称，自特朗普重新上任以来，外国政府已将 115 名美国公民从国外拘留中释放。白俄罗斯还释放了数百名政治犯，其中至少有 148 名政治犯的自由与与美国特使约翰·科尔和特朗普政府的谈判直接相关。 3 月份，在同一外交努力中，又有 250 名囚犯被赦免。
特朗普在中国领导人九月份访问华盛顿时向习近平提出了这些人的案件，支持者原本预计特朗普会在深圳再次这样做。特朗普在五月份访问北京时也曾敦促习近平释放陈。
中国当局于 2025 年 5 月 1 日指控陈从事间谍活动。他的妻子荣友芳表示，陈已因他的研究受到审问超过 100 次，她担心他会因捏造的罪名受审。
陈的工作由美国政府资助，公开且从未被保密。
“我知道特朗普总统已经两次要求习主席解决有林案，我希望中国政府能够在特朗普总统12月在佛罗里达州接待习主席之前这样做，”容周四告诉路透社。
据美国国务院称，敏津应中国政府邀请参加一个学术会议，于 6 月 3 日前往中国云南，随后被捕。路透社

Trump raises detention of Americans in China | The Straits Times
Trump says aide raised with Chinese side detention of two Americans
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
US President Donald Trump said an aide raised with Chinese officials the cases of two Americans detained by Beijing.
Published Nov 20, 2026, 06:25 AM
Updated Nov 20, 2026, 12:30 PM
Trump said an aide raised the detention of Americans Youlin Chen and Min Zin with Chinese officials during his Shenzhen summit with Xi.
Chen has been held since November 2024 and charged with espionage; Zin was arrested in June after visiting Yunnan for an academic conference.
Their cases matter because Washington calls them “wrongfully detained”, while China says it handles such cases under its own laws.
WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump on Nov 19 told Reuters that an aide raised with Chinese officials during his visit to China the cases of two Americans - Youlin Chen and Min Zin - designated by the US as wrongfully detained by Beijing.
Trump spoke to Reuters by phone as he flew back to Washington from his summit in Shenzhen with his Chinese and Russian counterparts.
Chen, a Chinese-born seismologist with expertise in detecting North Korean nuclear tests, has been held by China since November 2024; Zin, a researcher on Myanmar, was arrested during a visit to south-west China in June.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio designated both men as wrongfully detained, which makes obtaining their releases a US priority. China does not recognise the designation, and says detention cases are handled in accordance with its laws.
Republican lawmakers on Nov 18 had urged Trump to press Xi to free the pair. But Trump told Reuters that an aide had raised their cases with the Chinese side.
The men, he said, were among "a few" Americans being held by China.
"We’ve gotten a lot of them out, a lot of countries," Trump continued, referring to Americans released by other governments since he began his second term in January 2025.
"You know I’ve got hundreds of them out from Belarus and various other places."
Since Trump returned to office, foreign governments have freed 115 US citizens from detention abroad, according US officials. Belarus has also freed hundreds of political prisoners, including at least 148 whose freedom was directly linked to negotiations with US envoy John Coale and the Trump administration. Another 250 prisoners were freed in a March pardon that occurred amid the same diplomatic effort.
Advocates had expected Trump, who raised the men's cases with Xi when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, to do so again in Shenzhen. Trump also had urged Xi to release Chen when he visited Beijing in May.
Chinese authorities charged Chen with espionage on May 1, 2025. His wife, Youfang Rong, has said that Chen has been interrogated more than 100 times about his research and she expressed concern that he will be tried on concocted charges.
Chen's work has been funded by the US government, is publicly available and has never been classified.
"I know President Trump has already asked President Xi twice about resolving Youlin's case and I'm hopeful that the Chinese government will do this before President Trump hosts President Xi in Florida in December," Rong told Reuters on Thursday.
Min Zin was arrested after travelling to Yunnan, China, on June 3 after being invited by the Chinese government to attend an academic conference, according to the State Department. REUTERS

summary: 一名香港男子被判谋杀前女友，四年多前，她被发现死在豪华酒店房间的浴缸里。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四，即审判的第 14 天，32 岁的 Alex Lo 在高等法院被定罪，由 5 名男性和 2 名女性组成的七名陪审团达成了一致裁决。他被指控于2022年6月29日至30日在西九龙丽思卡尔顿酒店谋杀瑜伽教练Aqua Chow。周去世时年仅23岁。她原计划飞往美国参加瑜伽训练
content:
一名香港男子被判谋杀前女友，四年多前，她被发现死在豪华酒店房间的浴缸里。高等法院。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。周四，即审判的第 14 天，32 岁的 Alex Lo 在高等法院被定罪，由 5 名男性和 2 名女性组成的七名陪审团达成了一致裁决。他被指控于2022年6月29日至30日在西九龙丽思卡尔顿酒店谋杀瑜伽教练Aqua Chow。周去世时年仅23岁。 2022 年 6 月 30 日，她的尸体在酒店浴缸中被发现，当时她原定飞往美国参加瑜伽培训课程。法庭在庭审中获悉，罗与周于 2021 年 2 月成为情侣，并于次年 1 月分手，但仍保持联系。庭审期间，罗作证称，他因带周女士去高档餐厅、为她购买奢侈品而欠下了巨额债务，并表示自己非常爱她。他说，债务让他产生了自杀念头，因为贷款公司追着他还钱。周阿夸.照片：yoga.aqua，来自 Instagram。检方表示，经济负担是由罗某自行承担，郭启安法官则表示，他的情况本来是可以避免的。
对于罗说他有自杀念头的说法，郭问这些想法是否仍然是“一个想法”。他认为罗并不“认真”，因为有两次，当他作证想要自杀时，他给与周分手后开始交往的新女友打电话。还在审讯期间，罗作证说，他于2022年6月29日在油麻地购买的34厘米刀，是为了在酒店房间自杀而准备的。但他说，在一次争吵中，周告诉他他不是她终止的两次怀孕的父亲，他愤怒地“头脑爆炸”。他说他眼前一黑，只记得冲向她并刺伤了她。根据香港法律，谋杀罪被判处无期徒刑。该案押后至周五宣判。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong man has been found guilty of murdering his ex-girlfriend, more than four years after she was found dead in a bathtub in a luxury hotel room. High Court. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Alex Lo, 32, was convicted at the High Court on Thursday, the 14th day of his trial, after the seven-member jury – comprising five men and two women – arrived at the unanimous verdict. He had been charged with murdering yoga instructor Aqua Chow between June 29 and June 30, 2022, at the Ritz-Carlton in West Kowloon. Chow was 23 when she died. She had been scheduled to fly to the US for a yoga training course when her body was found in the hotel bathtub on June 30, 2022. The court heard during the trial that Lo and Chow became a couple in February 2021 and broke up the following January, although they stayed in touch. During the trial, Lo testified that he had run up enormous debt taking Chow to high-end restaurants and purchasing luxury items for her, saying he loved her very much. The debt left him suicidal, he said, as loan companies chased him to repay the money. Aqua Chow. Photo: yoga.aqua, via Instagram. The prosecution suggested that Lo had brought the financial burden onto himself, and Judge Kwok Kai-on said his situation could have been prevented. Regarding Lo’s statements that he felt suicidal, Kwok asked whether those thoughts remained “an idea.” He suggested Lo was not “serious” because on two occasions when he testified to wanting to take his own life, he had phoned his new girlfriend whom he began seeing after breaking up with Chow. Also during the trial, Lo testified that the 34-centimetre knife he bought in Yau Ma Tei on June 29, 2022, was meant for killing himself in the hotel room. But he said that amid an argument, in which Chow told him he was not the father of the two pregnancies she had terminated, his “mind exploded” in fury. He said he blacked out, and that all he remembered was charging towards her and stabbing her. Under Hong Kong law, murder carries a mandatory life term. The case was adjourned to Friday for the sentence to be handed down.

title: Compact and Covert
zh_title: 紧凑、隐蔽
source: 美国海军学院工作人员（大量国会报告每周2-3次）
summary: 法国土伦——法国海军的潜艇码头位于巴黎最大海军基地的有顶干船坞内和厚厚的混凝土墙后面。这个戒备森严的设施是核攻击潜艇中队最强大、最现代化的攻击艇的所在地，不被窥探。上个月，USNI News 参观了法国海军的一艘 Suffren 级核攻击潜艇 FS Duguay-Trouin (S636)，当时该潜艇正在进行维护。这艘核攻击潜艇于 2023 年服役，是法国海军 Suffren 级的第二艘，将成为法国海军的支柱。
content:
法国土伦——法国海军的潜艇码头位于巴黎最大海军基地的有顶干船坞内和厚厚的混凝土墙后面。这个戒备森严的设施是核攻击潜艇中队最强大、最现代化的攻击艇的所在地，不被窥探。上个月，USNI News 参观了法国海军的一艘 Suffren 级核攻击潜艇 FS Duguay-Trouin (S636)，当时该潜艇正在进行维护。这艘核攻击潜艇于 2023 年服役，是法国海军 Suffren 级的第二艘核潜艇，将成为未来几十年法国水下战争的支柱。 “对我们来说，冷战从未真正结束，”一位退役的法国海军潜艇指挥官在参观期间谈到他从 20 世纪 90 年代到 2010 年代的服役时光时说道。法国与北大西洋公约组织伙伴英国、德国和美国一起，一直在与俄罗斯海军进行水下对峙。从北大西洋的GIUK海峡到地中海沿岸，法国潜艇在日益恶化的安全局势中坚守岗位。随着俄罗斯对欧洲的威胁重新抬头，以及对法国在印度太平洋地区领土的新担忧，巴黎的攻击艇比以往任何时候都更加重要。这艘重 4,765 吨的潜艇停泊在有顶棚的干船坞内，让人们得以一睹法国海军旨在解决的能力和任务。
与现代中国、俄罗斯和美国的核攻击艇相比，紧凑型“苏弗伦”号的船员数量约为一半，排水量也显着减轻。紧凑型船员总数为 70 人，其中包括 15 名军官和 55 名士官，他们可以在鱼雷室后面的食堂享用面包店的新鲜法棍面包和配给的葡萄酒。 Duguay-Trouin 号的高度自动化特性可以从其武器舱中看出，攻击艇的执行官声称武器舱可由两名男子操作。与上一代红宝石级潜艇相比，萨弗伦级潜艇现在可以发射远程巡航导弹打击，承载专门的特种部队行动，并支持欧洲战区以外的扩展部署。从捍卫威慑到新的常规任务 2026 年 10 月 7 日，一艘拥有 38 年船龄的 FS Améthyste (S605) 核攻击艇在倾盆大雨中驶入土伦海军基地。USNI 新闻照片 灰色的阴天被土伦湾的倾盆大雨所取代。雨中出现了一艘潜艇的轮廓，指挥塔上挤满了模糊的人影。小船护送缓慢移动的 FS Améthyste (S605) 进入海湾。这艘冷战时期的攻击艇是法国红宝石级的最后一艘，也是法国海军服役的苏弗伦级之前的第一艘核攻击潜艇。与 Duguay-Trouin 相比，Améthyste 的排水量仅为 2,400 吨，并且是为不同时代而设计的。
与当时的西方和东方同类潜艇相比，红宝石级潜艇在武器装备和排水量上都明显较轻。这种设计理念反映了法国海军最初涉足核攻击艇及其在北大西洋和地中海的作战重点区域。冷战期间，法国海军的前线潜艇部队依赖于十几艘达芙妮级和阿戈斯塔级柴电推进攻击艇。 2026 年 10 月 6 日，SNLE Le Vigilant 首次发射 51.3 导弹。DGA 照片 核心任务之一

【原文 English Original】
TOULON, France — The French Navy’s submarine quay resides within covered dry docks and behind thick concrete walls at Paris’ largest naval base. Concealed from prying eyes, this closely guarded facility is home to the Squadron of Nuclear Attack Submarines’ most capable and modern attack boats. Last month, USNI News visited one of the French Navy’s Suffren-class nuclear attack submarines, FS Duguay-Trouin (S636), while the boat was undergoing maintenance. Commissioned in 2023, the nuclear attack submarine is the second of the sea service’s Suffren class and will form the backbone of French undersea warfare in the coming decades. “For us, the Cold War never really ended,” a retired French Navy submarine commander remarked during the tour about his time serving from the 1990s to 2010s. France, alongside North Atlantic Treaty Organization partners Britain, Germany and the U.S., has been engaged in a constant underwater standoff against the Russian Navy. From the North Atlantic waters of GIUK gap to the littorals of the Mediterranean, French submarines have stood guard amid an increasingly deteriorating security situation. With the resurgence of Russian threats to Europe and new concerns regarding French possessions in the Indo-Pacific, Paris’ attack boats are more relevant than ever. Resting within a covered dry dock, the 4,765-ton submarine provided a glimpse at the capabilities and missions that the French Navy aims to address. Compared to modern Chinese, Russian and American nuclear attack boats, the compact Suffren’s have roughly half the crew and displace considerably less weight. The compact crew complement of 70 personnel, divided between 15 officers and 55 petty officers, can enjoy their fresh baguettes from the bakery and wine ration at the mess behind the torpedo room. Duguay-Trouin’s highly automated nature can be seen within its weapons bay, which the attack boat’s executive officer claimed can be operated by two men. Compared to the previous generation of Rubis-class boats, the Suffren class can now launch long-range cruise missile strikes, host dedicated special forces operations and support extended-deployments beyond the European theater. From Defending the Deterrent to New Conventional Missions The 38-year-old FS Améthyste (S605) nuclear attack boat pulls into Toulon Naval Base under a torrential downpour on Oct. 7, 2026. USNI News photo A gray overcast sky gave way to a torrential downpour across Toulon Bay. A submarine silhouette emerged from the rain with hazy figures crowding the conning tower. Small boats escorted the slow moving FS Améthyste (S605) into the bay. The Cold War-era attack boat is the last of France’s Rubis-class, which was also the first class of nuclear attack submarines in French Navy service before the Suffren class. In contrast to Duguay-Trouin , Améthyste displaced only 2,400-tons and was created for a different era. Compared to its Western and Eastern counterparts at the time, Rubis-class submarines were notably lighter in both armament and displacement. This design philosophy reflected the French Navy’s initial foray into nuclear attack boats and its operational focus areas in the North Atlantic and Mediterranean. During the Cold War, the French Navy’s frontline submarine force relied on more than a dozen diesel-electric propelled attack boats from the Daphné and Agosta classes. The first firing of a 51.3 missile from the SNLE Le Vigilant on Oct. 6, 2026. DGA photo One of the core missions for the Rubis, and now Suffren class, was the escort of the French sea-based nuclear deterrent. Today, the French Navy operates four Triomphant-class submarines, each equipped with 16 M51 submarine-launched ballistic missiles. Alongside air-launched supersonic missiles carried by French Air Force and Navy Rafale fighters, the submarines form the pillars of Paris’ nuclear deterrent. France previously operated a full nuclear triad, but decommissioned its ground-based silos in the 1990s. On the morning of USNI News’ tour of Duguay-Trouin , France held its first at-sea test of a SLBM from FS Le Vigilant (S618) in the Atlantic Ocean. A M51.3 missile soared over the Atlantic in an event presided over by President Emmanuel Macron on a nearby frigate. French defense, military and industry leadership repeatedly highlighted this capability as Europe’s “only sovereign deterrent.” Aside from defending the country’s SSBNs, the Suffren-class brings new capabilities for French undersea warfare. At the front of the attack boat within its highly automated weapons room, the Suffren-class can deploy France’s first-ever submarine-launched cruise missiles. The domestic Naval Cruise Missile program’s roots can be traced to Paris’ failed attempt to procure Tomahawk cruise missiles from the U.S. in the early 2000s. Since 2017, the domestic long-range cruise missiles have enabled French frigates and submarines to strike targets out to 1,000 to 1,400 kilometers. Duguay-Trouin launches the cruise missiles from its four 533mm torpedo tubes. While French Navy frigates debuted the Naval Cruise Missile in combat during a joint operation with the U.S. and U.K. in 2018 against Syrian chemical weapon facilities, a Suffren-class sub first fired the cruise missile in a 2020 test. The FREMM Aquitaine and an SSN simultaneously fired an MdCN missile, shared in April of 2024. French Navy photo The initial production run of the Naval Cruise Missile only assembled 200 munitions, of which only 50 could be fired from the Suffren-class boats. However, the French military announced a new order for the latest variant of the cruise missile earlier this month at Euronaval 2026. This procurement comes amid a new focus by the French military in long-range precision fires influenced by lessons in the Ukraine conflict. Beyond conventional deep strike potential, the submarines also bring a new deployment method for French Navy special forces and the service’s growing hybrid fleet concept. A complement of Commando Marines can deploy from the submarine while submerged via a dry deck shelter module that can be attached for certain missions. The Suffren-class boats can also support swimmer delivery vehicles for these clandestine operations. Within the command center, 10 multi-functional display consoles flank an elevated captain’s seat and central tactical planning table. Each of these displays can be configured for different roles, a capability that can be useful depending on the mission tasked to Duguay-Trouin . French government-controlled shipbuilder Naval Group hopes to use submarines from the Suffren class and their command and control capabilities to support drone mesh networks in a hybrid fleet concept. At a demonstration at a nearby Naval Group facility, the shipbuilder showcased the potential benefits of operating extra-large unmanned underwater vehicles and aerial drones from the same consoles seen aboard Duguay-Trouin . The French Navy has already experimented with the deployment of UUVs, including a Spring 2026 test that saw the launch and recovery of a U.S. Navy Razorback UUV. In contrast to the highly autonomous vision of unmanned systems integration by fleets aboard, France is taking a more conservative force enabler approach in its hybrid fleet concept. French defense and industry officials want their drones to extend the surveillance reach of their manned assets. During the demonstration, the concept helped a French submarine detect targets in the Red Sea to enable an enhanced picture for a commander.

title: Navy Weapons Division to Make Tomahawk Components in 2027
zh_title: 海军武器部门将于 2027 年生产战斧部件
source: 美国海军学院工作人员（大量国会报告每周2-3次）
summary: 2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。一旦混音器上线
content:
2026 年 2 月 28 日，阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰小弗兰克·E·彼得森号 (DDG-121) 在支持史诗狂怒行动的行动中发射战斧对地攻击导弹。美国海军照片 海军空战中心武器部门上周宣布，将于 2027 年 6 月开始制造战斧巡航导弹弹头的组件，届时一种新型炸药和推进剂混合器上线。 11 月 9 日，由 B&P Littleford 制造的新型 300 加仑搅拌机在加利福尼亚州中国湖推进实验室举行剪彩仪式。 NAWCD 在一份新闻稿中表示，一旦混合器上线，NAWCD 的弹头生产团队将努力在制造商雷神公司需要弹头之前准备好弹头，帮助确保连续、准时地将战斧交付给舰队。 8月，海军授予雷神公司一份价值229亿美元的合同，以加速战斧生产，目标是每年生产1000多枚导弹。在“史诗狂怒行动”之后，国防部一直在努力增加和加速导弹和弹药的生产，该行动导致弹药迅速消耗。五角大楼的努力还集中于扩大制造商和供应商的国防工业基础，建设产能和冗余。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，来宾聚集在大型混合湾，观看中国湖推进实验室剪彩后新型 300 加仑混合机的演示。
一旦在 2027 年 6 月左右上线，混合器将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到为舰队生产战斧弹头的生产率。美国海军照片推进和能量部门负责人瑞安·亨特在新闻稿中表示，更快的生产需要更大的弹头容量。中国湖的海军实验室和马里兰州海军水面作战中心印度司令部表示，他们可以进行弹头的生产工作。目前，雷神公司是战斧制造的主要承包商，而通用动力军械和战术系统公司负责加工弹头箱，而 L3Harris 则为其装载炸药。 9 月，L3Harris 和 NAWCWD 签署了一项多年的公私合作伙伴关系，以制造导弹部件。亨特说，根据该协议，NAWCWD 计划生产部分战斧弹头。一年前，当 NAWCD 能源团队从博物馆取出一个战斧弹头盒时，NAWCD 开始了拥有制造战斧弹头能力的过程。能源团队将炸药和火箭推进剂混合，并将其装入海军武器中。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，中国湖推进实验室大型混合舱中，新型 300 加仑行星混合器的叶片位于混合碗上方。该混合器将于 2027 年 6 月左右投入使用，将使海军空战中心武器部门的能量团队达到舰队战斧弹头的生产率。
美国海军照片 该团队清理了箱子并混合了 PBXN-107 炸药并填充了 WDU-36/B 弹头。测试、成像和 X 射线证实该团队正确填充了它。经过这一努力，今年秋天，同一个团队填充了七个首件战斧弹头，这是新生产商建造的第一批用于检查的装置。能量处理部门负责人赞恩·戈德特表示，一旦通过，它们将成为“中国湖”的第一批生产弹头。弹头由中国湖运行了数十年的 150 加仑混合器填充，新的混合器将取代它。在演示构建过程中，团队还发现

【原文 English Original】
Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile during operations in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division will begin making a component for Tomahawk cruise missile warheads in June of 2027 when a new explosive and propellant mixer comes online, the division announced last week. A new 300 gallon mixer, built by B&P Littleford was inaugurated in a ribbon cutting ceremony on Nov. 9 at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory in California. Once the mixer is online, NAWCD’s warhead production team will work to have warheads ready before manufacturer Raytheon needs them, helping ensure continuous, on-time Tomahawk deliveries to the fleet, NAWCD said in a news release . In August, the Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion contract to accelerate Tomahawk production with a target of producing more than 1,000 missiles annually. The Department of Defense has been carrying out efforts to increase and accelerate productions of missiles and munitions following Operation Epic Fury, which has seen munitions rapidly expended. Pentagon efforts have also focused on expanding the defense industrial base of manufacturers and suppliers, building both capacity and redundancy. Guests gather in the large mix bay to watch a demonstration of a new 300-gallon mixer after its ribbon cutting at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo Faster production calls for more warhead capacity, said Ryan Hunter, head of the Propulsion and Energetics Division, in the release. Navy labs at China Lake and at Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division in Maryland said they could do the work to produce warheads. Currently, Raytheon is the prime contractor building Tomahawks while General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems machines the warhead cases and L3Harris loads them with explosives. In September, L3Harris and NAWCWD signed a multi-year public-private partnership to manufacture missile components. Under it, Hunter said, NAWCWD plans to produce a portion of the Tomahawk warheads. NAWCD began the process of having the capability to build Tomahawk warheads a year ago when the NAWCD energetics team pulled a Tomahawk warhead case out of a museum. The energetics team mixes explosives and rocket propellants and loads them into Navy weapons. The blades of a new 300-gallon planetary mixer rest above the mix bowl in the large mix bay at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. US Navy photo The team cleaned the case and mixed PBXN-107 explosive and filled the WDU-36/B warhead. Testing, imaging and X-rays confirmed the team filled it correctly. Following that effort, this fall, the same team filled seven first-article Tomahawk warheads, the first units a new producer builds for inspection. Once they pass, they become China Lake’s first production warheads, said Zane Goedert, head of the Energetics Processing Branch. The warhead was filled by a 150-gallon mixer China Lake has run for decades, which the new mixer will replace. During the demonstration build, the team also found the warhead specification needed a major update. Key parts and materials to address the issue can take up to a year to arrive, reads the NAWCD release. Patricia Hottowe, director of the Tomahawk Technical Project Office at NAWCWD, said in the release that the team spent much of the past year updating the specification and the approved supplier list. The Navy’s technical authority for the warhead must approve each new supplier and every future producer – Navy or industry – must build to that specification. NAWCWD also bought long-lead materials ahead of the multi-year contract, Hottowe said. A dozen new personnel have been hired to join the team, Goedert said. They will train under experienced technicians on safety, quality and procedures for about a year before working on their own. He added that loading the warhead is the easiest part while buying materials, bringing on people and getting answers are harder. Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Delbert D. Black (DDG-119) fires a Tomahawk Land Attack Missile (TLAM) in support of Operation Epic Fury, Feb. 28, 2026. US Navy photo The branch has filled warheads for the AGM-84H/K Stand-off Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (SLAM-E) missile since the mid-1990s. Goedert said his team routinely turns one-of-a-kind prototypes around on short timelines. That experience allowed the team to move faster on Tomahawk. According to Hunter, the challenge comes from a system built for fixed multi-year schedules. Now that system must move faster on a shorter clock. China Lake’s facilities will be able to meet that challenge due to its layout. “Because our plant is dispersed and because we will be curing the warheads in a different area than we’re casting them, we’re able to do simultaneous processes that will get higher throughput,” said Hunter. The plant’s newest buildings grew out of a rebuild as the July 2019 earthquakes destroyed three energetics compounds in the Salt Wells area of the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, reads the release. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command broke ground on their replacements, known as the trio, in April of 2022. Goedert said the team designed the Motor Assembly Compound to cut handling. Large rocket motors risk damage each time crews move them after casting. The same layout will speed warhead work. Rear Adm. Eric Gardner, principal deputy for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, spoke at the ribbon cutting and said the first-article warheads will lay the groundwork for China Lake to become an additional source of Tomahawk warhead production. “At PAE Munitions, we know that increasing weapons production takes more than contracts and funding,” Gardner said. “It takes people, infrastructure, materials, and strong partnerships across our Navy, our warfare centers and industry.”

title: Destroyer returns from 11-month-deployment
zh_title: 驱逐舰结束 11 个月的部署返回
summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《国防一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

【原文 English Original】
PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

title: Hong Kong sexual violence NGO flags ‘crucial room for improvement’ in sex crimes law overhaul
zh_title: 香港性暴力非政府组织指出性犯罪法改革有“重要的改进空间”
summary: 一家性暴力非政府组织表示，香港政府提议彻底修改该市已有数十年历史的性犯罪法律，其中包括一项允许被告声称他们错误地认为自己得到了同意的条款，这一提议仍然令人担忧。香港的性犯罪法已经数十年没有更新，而该市也出现了各种新型性侵犯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在周四的一份声明中，针对妇女的性暴力协会概述了对该法案的五个主要担忧，该法案于上周五在政府公报上发表。
content:
一家性暴力非政府组织表示，香港政府提议彻底修改该市已有数十年历史的性犯罪法律，其中包括一项允许被告声称他们错误地认为自己得到了同意的条款，这一提议仍然令人担忧。香港的性犯罪法已经数十年没有更新，而该市也出现了各种新型性侵犯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在周四的一份声明中，针对妇女的性暴力协会概述了对该法案的五个主要担忧，该法案于上周五在本月底进行立法审查之前在政府公报上发布。该协会表示：“虽然我们赞赏该法案纳入了我们的几项建议，包括引入针对持续性儿童性虐待的新罪行，但仍存在重要的改进空间，以确保改革真正反映和改善受害者幸存者的生活现实。” 《2026年性罪行法例（修订）条例草案》于今年七月首次提出。安全局表示，改革旨在审查该市已有数十年历史的性犯罪法律并使其更新，“以解决现行规定的不足之处，并应对与性犯罪相关的社会观念的变化”。担忧依然存在 在此次改革中，该非政府组织敦促政府纳入禁止被告在特定情况下声称“错误相信”同意的条款。
该协会列出了被告不能援引该辩护的11种情况——例如，受害者因中毒而失去知觉，因此无法表示同意。该协会表示，如果受害者受到暴力威胁或欺骗，也应被视为无法表示同意。由针对妇女的性暴力协会出版的关于性侵犯和性法律改革的小册子。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。它补充说，法院还应该通过考虑“被告为确定同意而实际所说或所做的事情”来确定错误信念是否合理。该非政府组织还表示，拟议的强奸罪应进行修改，以涵盖所有形式的口交性侵犯，“例如用嘴或舌头接触生殖器或肛门”，以确保法律对所有形式的口交性侵犯提供“平等的威慑和保护”。目前的法律草案仅涵盖一种形式的口交：用阴茎插入口腔。
该非政府组织表示，该法案还应将强奸罪重新命名为“未经同意的性侵”：“保留的术语‘强奸’——尤其是其中文对应词‘强奸’——带有严重的性别耻辱，阻碍了许多受害者幸存者寻求帮助。”该协会还建议强化持续性儿童性虐待罪，明确其追溯效力，并将事件门槛从法案中提出的三项行为降低至两项。该协会表示：“为了真正解决幸存者在回忆每起事件的具体细节方面所面临的困难，政府应借鉴其他司法管辖区的改革经验，将门槛提高到两项行为。”

【原文 English Original】
A sexual violence NGO has said that concerns remain over the Hong Kong government’s proposal to overhaul the city’s decades-old sex crimes laws, including over a provision allowing defendants to claim they mistakenly believed they were given consent. Hong Kong’s sexual offence laws have not been updated for dozens of years while the city saw various new types of sexual assault. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In a Thursday statement , the Association Concerning Sexual Violence Against Women outlined its five key concerns over the bill, which was published in the government gazette last Friday ahead of legislative scrutiny towards the end of the month. “While we appreciate that the Bill incorporates several of our recommendations, including the introduction of new offences addressing persistent child sexual abuse, there remains crucial room for improvement to ensure the reforms genuinely reflect and improve the lived realities of victim-survivors,” the association said. The Sexual Offences Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 was first put forward this July. The reforms aim to review the city’s decades-old sex crimes laws and bring them up to date, “to address the inadequacies of the current provisions and respond to changes in social perceptions related to sexual offences,” according to the Security Bureau. Concerns remain Under the overhaul, the NGO urged the government to include provisions barring a defendant from claiming a “mistaken belief” in consent under specific circumstances. The association listed 11 circumstances under which the accused should not be able to invoke that defence — for instance, where a victim was unconscious due to intoxication and therefore incapable of giving consent. Victims should also be considered incapable of giving consent if they were threatened with violence or deceived, the association said. Booklets published by Association Concerning Sexual Violence Against Women on sexual assault and sexual law reform. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The court should also determine whether a mistaken belief was reasonable by considering “what the accused actually said or did to ascertain consent,” it added. The NGO also said that the proposed rape offence should be amended to cover all forms of oral sexual assault “such as the application of the mouth or tongue to the genitalia or anus” to ensure that the law provides “equal deterrence and protection” against all forms of oral sexual assault. The draft law in its current form only covers one form of oral sexual assault: penetration of the mouth with the penis. The bill should also rename the rape offence to “sexual penetration without consent,” the NGO said: “The retained term ‘rape’ — and particularly its Chinese equivalent,「強姦」— carries a severe, gendered stigma that deters many victim-survivors from seeking help.” The association also suggested strengthening the persistent child sexual abuse offence by clarifying its retrospective effect and lowering the threshold of incidents from the three acts proposed in the bill to two. “To genuinely accommodate the difficulties survivors face in recalling the precise details of every single incident, the government should learn from the reform experiences from other jurisdictions and improve the threshold to two acts,” it said.

title: Xi Jinping’s Grandiose Timidity
zh_title: 习近平的胆大妄为
summary: 本周由中国国家主席习近平主持、唐纳德·特朗普、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京以及其他数十位领导人和名人出席的亚太经合组织峰会为中国提供了展示其外交影响力的机会。三个最大核大国的领导人从未聚在一起讨论世界事务，或他们利用其潜力或将其瓜分的计划。如果习近平想利用他的巨大影响力实现某些建设性目的，那么现在是一个很好的尝试时机。近千名记者报名观看现场盛况
content:
本周由中国国家主席习近平主持、唐纳德·特朗普、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京以及其他数十位领导人和名人出席的亚太经合组织峰会为中国提供了展示其外交影响力的机会。三个最大核大国的领导人从未聚在一起讨论世界事务，或他们利用其潜力或将其瓜分的计划。如果习近平想利用他的巨大影响力实现某些建设性目的，那么现在是一个很好的尝试时机。近 1000 名记者报名观看亚太经合组织峰会的盛况，其中一些人（比如我自己）飞越半个地球，观看历史从挤在一个地方的所有有权势的人身上浮现出来。但当所有的公开演讲都在深圳结束，所有的私下谈话都休会后，所有的一切都没有什么历史意义，这似乎就是主持人的意图。习近平避免就世界上最紧迫的危机进行任何公开辩论。他将峰会的议程限制在有关创新与合作的模糊陈述上，并让来访的记者徒劳地从他的声明中筛选出可能与活动潜力相匹配的新闻内容。至少白宫让我们的期望很低。在峰会前与记者的通话中，一位美国高级官员感叹中国不想谈论核武器控制。
这位官员表示：“我们确实认为，如果你愿意的话，中国现在是时候站到成年人的桌子上，就成年人的事情进行成年人的对话。”“他们不能只是拿着球回家。”习近平似乎不同意。他确保峰会看起来很重要，但不需要决定重要的事情。他与所有杰出嘉宾合影留念，同时避免他们的讨论出现在镜头前。峰会有可能在闭门会议上达成了一些协议，而参与者却选择保密。我们不知道，因为习近平确保世界只能看到经过净化的大国外交。中国观察家经常将他对平静的爱好归因于国民性格的各种特征：战略耐心、规避风险、乌龟的智慧战胜了鲁莽的西方兔子。但习近平本周拒绝做结束战争的混乱工作，看起来与其说是狡猾，不如说是胆怯。习近平对世界事务的影响力很大程度上源自中国的经济活力，而他不可能选择比深圳更好的地方来展示这种力量。两代人之前，这座城市只不过是香港海湾对面的一群渔村。如今，深圳人口约 1800 万（是曼哈顿的 10 倍多），是中国科技产业的中心和人工智能革命的引擎。当我周一到达时，这座城市已经进入峰会模式。
许多街道上的横幅都宣示了这次聚会的主题：开放创新合作。更诚实的口号可能包括“控制”一词。绵延数英里的警察路障包围了公园和林荫大道，阻止人们在 APEC 会场附近行走。我住的酒店大堂里有一个APEC咨询台，但后面友好的年轻人无法或不愿意告诉我APEC峰会将在哪里举行。他们只能分享 APEC 媒体中心的地址，该中心距离峰会几英里。整个大

【原文 English Original】
T he APEC summit , hosted this week by Chinese President Xi Jinping and attended by Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, among dozens of other leaders and luminaries, provided China with a chance to show its diplomatic heft. Never before had the leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers gathered to discuss the affairs of the world, or their plans to harness its potential or divide it up among themselves. If Xi wanted to use his enormous influence for some constructive purpose, this would have been a good time to try. Nearly 1,000 journalists signed up to see the spectacle at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, some of them (like myself) flying halfway around the world to watch history emerge from all of the powerful people packed into one place. But when all the public speeches had been made in Shenzhen and all the private talks adjourned, the sum of it amounted to nothing historic, which seemed to be the host’s intention. Xi avoided any public debate about the world’s most pressing crises. He confined the summit’s agenda to vague statements about innovation and cooperation, and he left the visiting journalists to sift in vain through his pronouncements for nuggets of news that might match the event’s potential. At least the White House kept our expectations low. In a pre-summit call with reporters, a senior U.S. official lamented that China did not want to talk about nuclear-arms control. “We do think it’s time for China to step up to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the official said. “They can’t just take their ball and go home.” Xi seemed to disagree. He made sure the summit looked important without needing to decide important things. He posed for a photo with all of his illustrious guests while keeping their discussions away from the cameras. It’s possible that behind closed doors, the summit resulted in deals that its participants have chosen to keep to themselves. We wouldn’t know, because Xi made sure the world could see only a sanitized version of great-power diplomacy. China watchers often attribute his fondness for the uneventful to various features of the national character: strategic patience, risk aversion, the wisdom of the tortoise over the reckless Western hare. But Xi’s refusal to do the messy work of ending wars looked a lot more timid than cunning this week. A lot of Xi’s power over world events derives from China’s economic dynamism, and he could not have chosen a better place than Shenzhen to put it on display. Two generations ago, the city was hardly more than a cluster of fishing villages across the bay from Hong Kong. Today, Shenzhen has a population of roughly 18 million people (more than 10 times that of Manhattan), and it serves as a hub of China’s tech industry and an engine of its AI revolution. By the time I arrived on Monday, the city had switched into summit mode. Banners on many streets proclaimed the themes of the gathering: Openness Innovation Cooperation . A more honest slogan might have included the word Control. Miles of police barricades surrounded parks and lined boulevards, preventing people from walking anywhere near the APEC venue. My hotel had an APEC information desk in the lobby, but the friendly young people behind it were unable or unwilling to tell me where the APEC summit would be held. They could share only the address of the APEC Media Center, located several miles away from the summit itself. Throughout the day, buses to the media center pulled up every few minutes at a gargantuan convention hall, which may go down in history as the most elaborate holding pen ever devised for the press. Inside, an army of minders provided us with every comfort—a limitless buffet of Chinese food, humanoid-robot baristas, massage chairs, and sleeping masks—but no access to the APEC summit or any of its noteworthy participants. Hundreds of reporters roamed around this space or sat scrolling on their phones. The more enterprising among them, determined to generate content, asked other reporters for interviews and filmed their opinions about the summit. Screens suspended above the media center showed footage from an APEC side event known as the CEO Summit. But there was no sound, and the QR code for the audio track led me to an error page that never finished loading. As my taxi slowed down near the entrance to the summit in Shenzhen, the self-styled “City of the Future,” Chinese policemen came running. Although I could not understand them, their shouting made me brace for a night in jail or the shock of a stun gun. Thankfully, my press credentials calmed the officers enough to let me approach their security checkpoint. But that’s as far as they let me go. Finally, on Wednesday afternoon, Trump gave headline writers something to work with. Descending the stairs of Air Force One, the U.S. president leaned in for a bro hug with Xi, who had come to greet his guest on the tarmac at the Shenzhen airport. By the placid standards of the summit, this qualified as breaking news, at least insofar as it placed Xi in a situation that he did not appear to have choreographed. From my place in the viewing stand, about a hundred yards away, it was impossible to hear what the two men briefly whispered to each other. [ Read: The deferential president ] T he next day , when Xi and Trump sat down with Putin for their first trilateral meeting, the Chinese leader opened with a statement about the Second World War and the need to avoid a third one in the future. But he did not bring up the two wars that his guests are currently fighting in Europe and the Middle East. Instead, he called for the United States, Russia, and China to create a nuclear-crisis hotline or, as he described it, “prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments are minimized.” The gesture showed a hint of openness from Xi to engage on nuclear issues with the Americans, though it fell far short of the disarmament talks that Trump and his predecessors have long sought with China. Earlier in the day, Xi’s speech to the summit stuck closely to the generic topics his government had plastered around town. The leaders gathered in Shenzhen must “expand mutual openness, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, extend opportunities for result-oriented cooperation across various fields, and strive to deliver more tangible results on the ground,” Xi told the summit’s opening banquet, according to the official translation. Make what you will of this verbiage, but it did not exude an eagerness on China’s part to roll up its sleeves and fix the planet’s problems. Wealth and status, of course, do not necessitate any particular willingness to act. No one expects the sultan of Brunei, another guest at APEC this week, to resolve conflicts or reduce the likelihood of Armageddon. But the leader of a superpower, whether ascendant or established, does bear some responsibility for engaging in matters of war and peace, and Xi showed little interest in carrying that burden this week. Maybe that is for the best. Few would want China to project its power the way Russia has done in recent years, through brutality against its neighbor and thuggery just about everywhere else. But Putin does not portray himself as a benevolent force in the world. He has been candid about his desire to tear apart the Western order and rebuild it to his liking. Xi cultivates a different image. He tries to be seen, in contrast to Putin and Trump, as a force for stability, a convener of nations and steward of the status quo. To his credit, he has reportedly talked Putin down from using nuclear weapons in Ukraine. But that does not make him a peacemaker. Nearly five years into the war, Xi has done little to stop it. He has continued selling the technology that Ukraine and Russia use to manufacture weapons, apparently content to let their conflict weaken Europe and transform Moscow into an economic vassal of Beijing. [ Read: NATO’s nightmare ] Nor has Xi spent much political capital on ending the war in Iran, whose regime has relied on trade with China to rebuild its arsenal and continue fighting. In his rhetoric and public actions, Xi has done his best to keep a distance from these wars, pretending that they are none of China’s business. He has abstained from all organized efforts to mediate peace, perhaps because these efforts continue falling flat. In fairness to Xi, most leaders would rather not associate themselves with intractable conflicts and diplomatic failures. But he can’t really have it both ways. He can’t host the presidents of the two nuclear superpowers, both of whom are waging wars against far smaller nations, without offering any public thoughts about those wars or the possible paths to their conclusion. He can’t invite his chief rivals in the race to create intelligent machines and then elide the topic of this race and the threats it poses to humanity. Failing to contend in any outward way with these era-defining problems suggests that Xi does not aim to exercise power. He aims to hoard it and put it on display.

title: Beijing bolsters South China Sea push with new island runway: analysts
zh_title: 北京通过新岛屿跑道加强南海推进：分析人士
summary: 根据专家和法新社看到的卫星图像，中国正在有争议的南海另一个岛屿上修建一条跑道，这可能会大大加强其在战略水道上的军事足迹。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 10 月 17 日拍摄的讲义卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁上的一个港口的基础。照片：星球实验室/法新社。北京声称对南海大部分地区拥有主权，尽管国际裁决认为其主张没有法律依据，而且与几个国家经常发生对抗
content:
根据专家和法新社看到的卫星图像，中国正在有争议的南海另一个岛屿上修建一条跑道，这可能会大大加强其在战略水道上的军事足迹。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 10 月 17 日拍摄的讲义卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁上的一个港口的基础。照片：星球实验室/法新社。北京声称对南海大部分地区拥有主权，尽管国际裁决认为其主张没有法律依据，而且与几个东南亚国家就西沙群岛和南沙群岛的控制权经常发生对抗。这两个岛链基本上都是由珊瑚礁和露头组成，但分析人士表示，中国一直在稳步填海造地和建设基础设施，以获得对海洋的军事控制权。美国战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）和洛伊研究所在最近的详细报告中援引卫星图像称，北京去年年底开始在西沙群岛羚羊礁进行大规模疏浚和填海造地，中国、越南和台湾均声称对该群岛拥有主权。洛伊研究所报告的作者洛厄尔·鲍蒂斯塔告诉法新社，中国在 10 个月内将西沙群岛的珊瑚礁从最小的西沙群岛前哨基地之一转变为可以与最大的环礁相媲美的岛屿。
羚羊礁上近三公里的跑道将是北京在西沙群岛的第二条跑道，与南沙群岛和海南岛上的基础设施一起，有助于“建立一个跨越大海的跑道、港口和传感器的综合网络”，包蒂斯塔说。1974年，中国和越南在西沙群岛发生了一场短暂但血腥的小冲突。70多名越南士兵被杀，从那时起，中国实际上控制了这些岛屿。据战略与国际研究中心称，该跑道的大小与西沙群岛永兴岛和南沙群岛其他三个机场的跑道相似。分析人士表示，羚羊角沿西北-东南轴线约六公里，可能成为中国在南海最重要的前哨基地之一，有可能帮助北京在发生冲突时限制美国及其盟国海军的进入。中国表示，西沙群岛的开发是出于民用目的，并补充说，西沙群岛的居民人口较少，主要是渔民。外交部发言人三月份表示，中国在该岛的填海造地活动是“必要的建设”，目的是“改善岛上的生活和工作条件，发展当地经济”。运输机、轰炸机 在地球成像公司 Planet Labs 9 月份拍摄的照片中，清晰可见一个看起来像跑道的结构。
这些图像是日本情报公司 Deep Dive 最近报告的一部分，法新社也看到了这些图像。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 11 月 8 日拍摄的分发卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁。照片：星球实验室/法新社。 Deep Dive 主任、前驻中国武官 Bonji Ohara 在报告中表示，该结构不仅能够容纳战斗机，还能够容纳更大型的飞机，包括运输机、空中加油机和轰炸机。他说，新跑道可能会让中国更接近实现“对整个南海的完全控制”。 CSIS 表示，Antelope 可以增强中国传感能力的覆盖范围

【原文 English Original】
China is building a runway on another island in the disputed South China Sea that could significantly strengthen its military footprint in the strategic waterway, according to experts and satellite images seen by AFP. This handout satellite image taken by Planet Labs PBC on October 17, 2026 shows the foundations of a harbour on the disputed Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. Photo: Planet Labs/AFP. Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis, and confrontations have occurred regularly with  several Southeast Asian nations over control of the Paracel and Spratly islands. Both island chains are essentially made up of reefs and outcrops, but analysts say China has been steadily reclaiming land and building infrastructure to gain military control of the sea. Beijing late last year began large-scale dredging and reclaiming land at Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands, which are claimed by China, Vietnam and Taiwan, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and the Lowy Institute said in recent detailed reports, citing satellite images. Lowell Bautista, author of the Lowy Institute report, told AFP that China transformed the reef in 10 months from one of its smallest Paracel outposts into an island that can rival its largest atoll. The nearly three-kilometre runway on Antelope Reef would be Beijing’s second in the Paracels and — together with infrastructure on the Spratly Islands and on Hainan island — helps “create an integrated network of runways, harbours and sensors stretching across the sea”, Bautista said. China and Vietnam fought a brief but bloody skirmish over the Paracels in 1974. More than 70 Vietnamese soldiers were killed and China has had de facto control over the islands since then. The runway is a similar size to an airstrip on the Paracels’ Woody Island and three others across the Spratlys, according to CSIS. Analysts say Antelope — which is around six kilometres along its northwest-southeast axis — could become one of China’s most important outposts in the South China Sea, potentially helping Beijing limit the access of US and allied naval forces in the event of conflict. China says the development of the Paracel Islands, which it adds have a small resident population of mostly fishers, is for civilian purposes. A spokesperson for the foreign ministry said in March that China’s land reclamation activities there are “necessary construction” for “improving living and working conditions on the islands and growing the local economy”. Transport planes, bombers A structure that appears to be a runway is clearly visible in photos taken in September by Earth imaging company Planet Labs. The images were reviewed as part of a recent report by Japanese intelligence firm Deep Dive and were also seen by AFP. This handout satellite image taken by Planet Labs PBC on November 8, 2026 shows the disputed Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. Photo: Planet Labs/AFP. Deep Dive director Bonji Ohara, a former defence attache in China, said in the report that the structure would be able to handle not just fighter jets but also larger aircraft, including transport planes, aerial refuelling tankers and bombers. The new runway could potentially bring China closer to achieving “full control over the entire South China Sea”, he said. The CSIS has said that Antelope could enhance the reach of Chinese sensing capabilities closer to Vietnam’s shores and help expand its military capacity in an area of the northern South China Sea which is close to major shipping lanes. Antelope Reef’s runway is expected to be operational by mid-2027, although other analysts were more cautious about its significance. The runway and harbour will “add additional capacity and resilience to the facility that enable China’s military and paramilitary operations in the South China Sea,” Harrison Pretat, deputy director at CSIS’s Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, told AFP. But “Southeast Asian claimants have still largely maintained access to offshore resources and occupy their own outposts,” he said. Limited pushback Nevertheless, Pretat warned that “international attention and pushback… has been far less than might be expected given the scale and significance” of construction, due in part “to distraction from other global crises”. “Regional countries…along with the United States and the international community, should be speaking with a stronger voice against island building and other attempts to permanently alter conditions in disputed areas,” he said. Vietnam in August called construction at Antelope Reef “completely illegal” and demanded “such activities cease immediately”. And in October, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said that China’s military build-up was creating a “condition of pressure” in Southeast Asia, and urged allies and partners to deepen cooperation. But Hunter Marston of the Lowy Institute told AFP that “ASEAN (member states) will never be capable of communicating with one voice” due partly to their different views of China. A crew member of the China Coast Guard vessel 5205 removes the cover of a 70 mm cannon and aims it toward the BRP Teresa Magbanua near Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea in August 2022. File photo: Philippine Coast Guard. US ally the Philippines has been engaged in years of confrontations with China over disputed areas of the sea, and Filipino and Chinese ships have engaged in repeated confrontations in recent years, some leading to collisions and injuries. Ohara said that Beijing views the sea as “a sanctuary… where it does not want foreign powers to enter in the event of a contingency” in the region. “While it will not restrict freedom of navigation in peacetime, if some incident occurs, China intends to prevent not only US naval forces but also those of its allies — for example, Australian submarines — from entering,” he said.

title: USNI News Western Pacific Pulse: Nov. 13, 2026
zh_title: USNI 新闻西太平洋脉搏：2026 年 11 月 13 日
source: 美国海军学院工作人员（大量国会报告每周2-3次）
summary: 以下是上周西太平洋主要舰船活动和演习的摘要。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，新加坡，一名隶属于第 137 电子攻击中队 (VAQ) 的美国水手在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 机库湾对 E/A-18G 咆哮者进行维护。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群于周日从新加坡出发。该打击群包括西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰（CVN-71）及其第11舰载机联队（CVW）、长津号巡洋舰（CG-65）和保罗·汉密尔顿号驱逐舰（DDG-6）
content:
以下是上周西太平洋主要舰船活动和演习的摘要。 2026 年 11 月 9 日，新加坡，一名隶属于第 137 电子攻击中队 (VAQ) 的美国水手在尼米兹级航空母舰西奥多·罗斯福号 (CVN-71) 机库湾对 E/A-18G 咆哮者进行维护。美国海军照片 西奥多·罗斯福号航母打击群于周日从新加坡出发。该打击群包括西奥多·罗斯福号航空母舰（CVN-71）及其第11舰载机联队（CVW）、长津号巡洋舰（CG-65）以及保罗·汉密尔顿号驱逐舰（DDG-60）和迪凯特号（DDG-73）。西奥多·罗斯福、长津和迪凯特向西航行进入马六甲海峡，而保罗·汉密尔顿则向东航行进入南中国海。西奥多·罗斯福号、长津号和迪凯特号目前正在印度洋前往美国中央司令部。日本横须贺附近 印度海军 Shivalik 级隐形多用途护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F 49)、日本海上自卫队日向级直升机驱逐舰 JS Ise (DDH 182)、最上级护卫舰 JS Mogami (FFM 1)、澳大利亚皇家海军安扎克级护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) 和美国海军 San 2026 年 11 月 7 日，安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞运输舰安克雷奇号 (LPD-23) 和约翰·穆萨号 (LPD-26) 在 2026 年马拉巴尔演习期间在西太平洋编队航行。美国海军照片 2026 年马拉巴尔四方演习于周四在日本横须贺附近海域结束。
参与的资产包括日本海上自卫队直升机驱逐舰 JS Ise (DDH-182)、护卫舰 JS Mogami (FFM-1)、日本海上自卫队潜艇和 P-1 海上巡逻机 (MPA)、印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri (F49)、澳大利亚皇家海军护卫舰 HMAS Stuart (FFH153) 和澳大利亚皇家空军 P-8A Poseidon MPA、美国海军 P-8A 海神 MPA 和两栖运输船坞 USS Anchorage (LPD-23) 和 USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26)。安克雷奇号和约翰·P·穆萨号与两栖攻击舰马金岛号 (LHD-8) 以及已登船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队组成了马金岛两栖待命大队。据当地船舶观察员称，这三艘船均于周六从横须贺舰队活动司令部（CFAY）出发。 2026 年 11 月 8 日，在日本横须贺，美国海军陆战队海军陆战队海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364（加强型）的飞行员从圣安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞舰安克雷奇 (LPD-23) 的飞行甲板上驾驶一架 MV-22B 鱼鹰。美国海军照片安克雷奇于周五返回横须贺，目前停泊据当地船舶观察员称，那里近海。据当地船舶观察员称，澳大利亚皇家海军斯图尔特号护卫舰在参加 2026 年马拉巴尔演习后于周四返回横须贺。据当地船舶观察员称，印度海军护卫舰 INS Sahyadri 于周四返回横须贺，并于周五离开。
据当地船舶观测员称，潜艇补给船弗兰克·凯布尔号 (AS-40) 于周三驶入横须贺指挥官舰队活动基地。在西太平洋，隶属于海军陆战队中型倾转旋翼机中队 (VMM) 364 的美国海军陆战队 CH-53 种马准备从圣安东尼奥级两栖运输船坞舰约翰·P·穆萨号 (LPD-26) 的飞行甲板起飞， 2026 年 11 月 9 日。美国海军照片 两栖攻击舰马金岛号和两栖运输船坞约翰·P·穆萨号正在美国第七舰队作战区域航行。在菲律宾海 台湾民族党秘书长吴钊燮于 2026 年 11 月 12 日发布的图片

【原文 English Original】
The following is a summary of major ship movements and exercises in the Western Pacific over the last week. In Singapore A U.S. sailor assigned to Electronic Attack Squadron (VAQ) 137 conducts maintenance on an E/A-18G Growler in the hangar bay of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71), Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group departed on Sunday from Singapore. The strike group includes aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) with embarked carrier air wing (CVW) 11, cruiser USS Chosin (CG-65) and destroyers USS Paul Hamilton (DDG-60) and USS Decatur (DDG-73). Theodore Roosevelt , Chosin and Decatur sailed west to enter the Malacca Strait while Paul Hamilton sailed east into the South China Sea. Theodore Roosevelt , Chosin and Decatur are now in the Indian Ocean en route to U.S. Central Command. Near Yokosuka, Japan Indian Navy Shivalik-class stealth multi-role frigate INS Sahyadri (F 49), Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Hyuga-class helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH 182), Mogami-class frigate JS Mogami (FFM 1), Royal Australian Navy Anzac-class frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH 153) and U.S. Navy San Antonio-class amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26) sail in formation in the Western Pacific Ocean during Exercise Malabar 2026, Nov. 7, 2026. US Navy photo Quad Exercise Malabar 2026 wrapped up Thursday in the waters near Yokosuka, Japan. Participating assets were Japan Maritime Self Defense Force helicopter destroyer JS Ise (DDH-182), frigate JS Mogami (FFM-1), a JMSDF submarine and a P-1 Maritime Patrol Aircraft (MPA), Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri (F49), Royal Australian Navy frigate HMAS Stuart (FFH153) and a Royal Australian Air Force P-8A Poseidon MPA, a U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon MPA and amphibious transport docks USS Anchorage (LPD-23) and USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26). Anchorage and John P. Murtha with amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD-8) and the embarked 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit form the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. All three ships departed Saturday from Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), according to local ship spotters . In Yokosuka, Japan U.S. Marine Corps Marines, pilots assigned to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364 (Reinforced), fly an MV-22B Osprey from the flight deck aboard San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS Anchorage (LPD-23), Nov. 8, 2026. US Navy photo Anchorage returned to Yokosuka on Friday and is currently anchored offshore there, according to local ship spotters . RAN frigate HMAS Stuart returned on Thursday to Yokosuka after its participation in Exercise Malabar 2026, according to local ship spotters . Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri returned on Thursday to Yokosuka and departed on Friday, according to local ship spotters . Submarine tender USS Frank Cable (AS-40) pulled into Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka on Wednesday, according to local ship spotters . In the Western Pacific A U.S. Marine Corps CH-53 Stallion, attached to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 364, prepares to take off from the flight deck aboard San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS John P. Murtha (LPD-26), Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo Amphibious assault ship Makin Island and amphibious transport dock John P. Murtha are underway in U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations. In the Philippine Sea A graphic posted Nov. 12, 2026, by Joseph Wu, Secretary General of Taiwan’s National Security Council. Taiwan National Security Council graphic The People’s Liberation Army Navy Liaoning CSG is operating in the Philippine Sea waters east of the Philippine island of Samar as of Thursday, according to a graphic posted by Joseph Wu, Secretary General of Taiwan’s National Security Council. The CSG was last visually sighted in October. The Liaoning CSG previously included aircraft carrier CNS Liaoning (16) cruisers CNS Anshan (101) and CNS Wuxi (104) and destroyer CNS Huainan (123) but the accompanying ships to the carrier may have changed since. In the South China Sea (L-R) Able Seaman Maritime Logistic – Supply Chain Leah Locke and Able Seaman Maritime Logistic – Supply Chain Grace Reading lay wreaths during a wreath laying ceremony for Remembrance Day during a Regional Presence Deployment 2026 on Nov. 10, 2026. Australian Defense photo Royal Australian Navy fleet oiler HMAS Stalwart (A304) is operating in the South China Sea waters near Brunei on the Royal Australian Navy’s regional presence deployment. On Wednesday , the ship conducted a Remembrance Day wreath laying ceremony with Royal Brunei Navy offshore patrol vessel KDB Darulaman (08). In Guam The ROKN Joint Cruise Training Task Force, 741 second year cadets from three service academies and the Armed Forces Nursing Academy were in Guam for a port visit on Nov. 9, 2026. US Navy photo The ROKN Joint Cruise Training Task Force, 741 second year cadets from three service academies and the Armed Forces Nursing Academy were in Guam as of Monday on a port visit. The task force includes amphibious assault ship ROKS Marado (LPH-6112) and amphibious landing ships ROKS Ilchulbong (LST-688) and ROKS Nojeokbong (LST-689), along with embarked Republic of Korea Marine Corps (ROKMC) MUH-1 Marineon helicopters. In Kangwon Province, North Korea North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Nov. 11, 2026, in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province. State media Korea Central News Agency photo North Korea leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction site of a new naval base on Wednesday in Thongchon County, Kangwon Province, located on North Korea’s east coast, state media Korean Central News Agency reported. In Maizuru, Japan Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Nov. 10, 2026. JMSDF photo Royal Navy offshore patrol vessel HMS Spey (P234) departed JMSDF Maizuru Naval Base on Tuesday after completing a five-day port visit that began on Nov. 6. Spey with sister ship HMS Tamar (P233) are forwarded deployed to the Indo-Pacific. Near Yonaguni Island and Taiwan A Chinese BZK-005 reconnaissance UAV on Nov. 11, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Wednesday, a suspected Chinese Unmanned Aerial Vehicle flew in from the East China Sea, passed between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan and reached the Philippine Sea. The UAV then turned back when it reached a point east of the northeast tip of Taiwan and flew between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan to return to the East China Sea. Fighter aircraft from the Japan Air Self-Defense Force Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. Also on Wednesday, a Chinese BZK-005 reconnaissance UAV flew in from the East China Sea, passing between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan to enter the Philippine Sea. The drone then flew south until it was east of the northwest tip of Taiwan and conducted a circuit flight before returning back the same way to the East China Sea. JASDF fighter aircraft from the JASDF Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled in response. Suspected Chinese UAV flight paths on Nov. 11, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office map On Thursday, a suspected Chinese UAV flew in from the East China Sea and entered the Philippine Sea, flying between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan. The suspected drone was east of the northeast tip of Taiwan before its track was lost. Later that same day, another suspected Chinese UAV was tracked from the Philippine Sea east of the northeast tip of Taiwan. The UAV flew north and entered the East China Sea after flying between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan. Japan’s Joint Staff Office issued a news release on the flights, indicating the flights were conducted by different UAVs. Fighter aircraft from the JASDF Southwestern Air Defense Command were scrambled to intercept. In the East China Sea A Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo On Tuesday, a Chinese Y-9 Electronic Intelligence aircraft flew in from China and flew from an area south of the Danjo Islands in the East China Sea to a position northwest of Okinawa. After completing a patrol circuit, the Y-9 flew back to China. In response, JASDF fighter aircraft were scrambled. In the Miyako Strait PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fast combat support ship CNS Hulunhu (901) on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo PLAN destroyer CNS Qiqihar (121) and fast combat support ship CNS Hulunhu (901) were spotted on Thursday sailing south 60 kilometers – 37 miles – west of Kume Island. The ships sailed southeast between Okinawa and Miyako Island to enter the Philippine Sea. A JMSDF P-1 MPA of Fleet Air Wing 1 and a JMSDF P-3C Orion MPA shadowed the PLAN ships. In La Pérouse Strait A Russian Navy Kilo-class submarine, amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov on Nov. 10, 2026. Japan Joint Staff Office photo A Russian Navy Kilo-class submarine, amphibious landing ship RFS Nikolai Vilkov (081) and tugboat Fotiy Krylov were sighted sailing west 40 kilometers – 25 miles – northeast of Cape Soya on the main island of Hokkaido late Tuesday. From Tuesday to Wednesday, the submarine and ships sailed west through La Pérouse Strait, which separates Hokkaido from Russia’s Sakhalin Island, to enter the Sea of Japan. JMSDF fast attack craft JS Umitaka (PG-828) and a JMSDF P-3C Orion MPA shadowed the Russian submarine and ships. This post was written by Dzirhan Mahadzir.

title: Hong Kong whistleblower of student app scandal charged with doxxing
zh_title: 香港学生应用程序丑闻举报人被控人肉搜索
summary: 一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。一个
content:
一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。根据指控书，程被指控披露四名未透露姓名的人（X、Y、Z 和 A）的个人数据。据称，她这样做的目的是为了对这些人或其家人造成特定伤害，或者不顾后果地考虑是否会造成伤害。程被指控在未经“X”同意的情况下，披露了“X”的中英文全名、她的年龄、学校、学年、家庭关系、社交媒体资料、照片、居住区域、资格和行程。据称，她还披露了其他三人的个人信息，包括姓名、照片和家庭关系。 Y 的出生日期被泄露，Z 的住所被泄露，A 的社交媒体资料被泄露。
周三，郑在东区裁判法院出庭，在首席裁判官苏泽豪面前出庭，无需答辩。裁判官批准了辩方休庭寻求法律意见的请求，以及控方为受害者申请匿名令的申请。案件押后至12月23日审理。文件显示，郑以3,000港元现金保释。 2025 年 6 月，Cheng 担心 MediSafe（一款荣获多项奖项的药物处方应用程序）实际上并非由中学生 Clarisse Poon 制作，引发了病毒式的学术诚信丑闻。一家名为 AI Health Studio 的美国软件开发公司后来表示，该应用程序是受潘的母亲委托开发的，并且该应用程序未经其同意就提交给了比赛。早些时候被捕 这名大学生二月份在社交媒体上表示，她因举报事件而被捕。在八月份的一份声明中，她说她拒绝保释并被无条件释放。拒绝更新保释是指一个人拒绝接受延长保释期限并要求警方正式指控或释放他们的程序。警方稍后仍可以重新逮捕并指控嫌疑人。东部裁判法院。照片：何凯莉/HKFP。四月，程面临亲北京支持者要求被城大开除的呼吁。
香港编程协会 Facebook 群组的一名匿名成员当月发布了请愿书，敦促“香港庞大的蓝营”分享该请愿书。请愿书还表示，签名者将与警方、国家安全部门和中联办等当局联系，要求将她驱逐。据当时的当地媒体报道，在最初披露的三个月后，这家委托的软件公司证实了其参与，随后该学生的父母——著名肝病专家 Ronnie Poon 和 Roberta Pang——表示，他们的女儿将归还与 MediSafe 相关的所有奖项。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong woman who sparked a viral academic integrity controversy after questioning the legitimacy of a secondary student’s award-winning app has been charged with doxxing. Hailey Cheng. Photo: Hailey Cheng, via Facebook. Hailey Cheng faces four counts of disclosing personal data without a data subject’s consent causing specified harm, according to court documents dated Wednesday. Cheng, a former student at the City University of Hong Kong now admitted to Columbia University in New York, said on Threads the same day that the case had been mentioned in court and that she was granted bail . According to the charge sheet, Cheng was charged with disclosing personal data of four unnamed people referred to as X, Y, Z, and A. She allegedly did so with an intent to cause specified harm to those people or their family members, or being reckless as to whether the harm would be caused. Cheng was accused of disclosing the full English and Chinese names of “X,” her age, school, school year, family relationships, social media profiles, photos, living area, qualifications, and itinerary, without her consent. She also allegedly disclosed personal information of the other three people, including their names, photos, and family relationships. The person known as Y had her date of birth disclosed, while Z had his residence leaked, and the individual known as A had her social media profile disclosed. Cheng appeared before Chief Magistrate Victor So at the Eastern Magistrates’ Courts on Wednesday and was not required to enter a plea. The magistrate granted the defence’s request for an adjournment to seek legal advice and the prosecution’s application for an anonymity order for the victims. The case was adjourned to December 23. According to the document, Cheng was released on a HK$3,000 cash bail. In June 2025, Cheng raised concerns that MediSafe – a medication prescription app that won multiple awards – was not actually made by secondary school student Clarisse Poon, triggering a viral academic integrity scandal. A US-based software development company called AI Health Studio later said it was commissioned by Poon’s mother to build the app, and that the app was submitted to competitions without its consent. Earlier arrest The university student said on social media in February that she had been arrested in relation to the whistleblowing incident. In an August statement, she said that she refused bail and was released unconditionally. Refusing to renew bail is a procedure where a person declines to accept an extension of bail terms and requires the police to either formally charge or release them. The police can still re-arrest and charge the suspect later. Eastern Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. In April, Cheng faced calls from pro-Beijing supporters to be expelled from CityU. An anonymous member of a Facebook group for the Hong Kong Programming Society posted the petition that month urging “Hong Kong’s vast blue camp” to share it. The petition also said that signatories would be in touch with the authorities, including the police, its National Security Department, and Beijing’s Liaison Office to demand her expulsion. Three months after the original revelation, the commissioned software company confirmed its involvement, following which the student’s parents – renowned liver disease specialist Ronnie Poon and Roberta Pang – said their daughter would return all the awards associated with MediSafe, according to local media reports at the time.

title: US rare earths regulations to get stricter in the new year
zh_title: 新的一年美国稀土监管将更加严格
source: MINING.COM 全球矿业（稀土/关键矿产）
summary: 美国正准备对交付五角大楼的稀土产品实施更严格的监管，迫使国防承包商从 2027 年 1 月 1 日起淘汰来自中国、朝鲜、伊朗和俄罗斯的材料，此举将重新设计供应链，即使现在没有资源这样做。为了摆脱对中国和其他国家关键矿产的依赖，国防承包商将不再能够销售在这四个被禁国家开采、精炼或分离的五角大楼磁铁、钽或钨产品，即使最终完成
content:
美国正准备对交付五角大楼的稀土产品实施更严格的监管，迫使国防承包商从 2027 年 1 月 1 日起淘汰来自中国、朝鲜、伊朗和俄罗斯的材料，此举将重新设计供应链，即使现在没有资源这样做。为了摆脱对中国和其他国家关键矿产的依赖，国防承包商将不再能够销售在这四个被禁国家开采、精炼或分离的五角大楼磁铁、钽或钨产品，即使成品是在其他地方完成的。现有规则允许部分原材料来自中国，只要最终熔化或生产发生在其他地方。这些变化影响了用于电动汽车、航空航天和风力涡轮机的钕铁硼磁铁。钐钴磁铁、钽金属和钨产品由于耐热，对航空航天和国防至关重要，也将受到并行限制的影响。这个最后期限可能会暴露华盛顿减少对中国矿产依赖的努力与该行业替代这些矿产的能力之间的差距。尽管联邦政府投资了数百万美元，但美国在多个生产阶段都缺乏足够的产能，导致制造商面临潜在的供应中断。
这些限制源于 2019 年针对五角大楼对来自受关注国家的关键材料的依赖而出台的立法。初步措施涵盖钕铁硼磁铁、钐钴磁铁和​​钨产品，这些产品首先受到影响。此后，限制逐年变得更加严格，涵盖的产品也越来越多，直到 2024 年设定了 2027 年的最后期限。唐纳德·特朗普总统的第 14415 号行政命令强制执行了最后期限，并规定了对承包商的期望。它需要供应链测绘和尽职调查、替代供应来源的资格以及在禁止从相关国家采购某些关键金属和稀土磁体的情况下限制可用的豁免。收紧规则还超出了稀土磁体的范围。镓和锗是下一个从 2027 年 12 月 18 日开始受到限制的金属。关键矿产安全与长达数十年的矿山时间表相冲突。中国控制着这些关键矿产的大部分加工，并且自己也制定了限制。该国于2025年4月对稀土出口实行更严格的限制，该限制自当年10月起暂停。该禁令将于 2027 年 1 月 10 日解除，即美国监管变化开始仅 9 天后。满足需求的投资自宣布这一新的监管变化以来，美国一直在该行业进行数百万美元的投资。
尽管许多项目和设施已获得充足资金，但尚未准备好投入商业生产。问题仍然存在，即采矿能力、分离能力、金属化和成品磁体生产是美国尚未有能力完成的四个不同步骤。据《环境与能源领袖》报道，如果产品在整个生产过程中的任何时候经过某个覆盖国家，这些产品仍然可能无法通过 DFARS 测试。美国一直在尝试与其他可以成为稀土和其他重要矿产供应国的国家进行接触，例如缅甸、马来西亚

【原文 English Original】
The US is getting ready to impose stricter regulations on rare earths products delivered to the Pentagon, forcing defence contractors to eliminate materials sourced from China, North Korea, Iran and Russia starting Jan. 1, 2027, in a move that redesigns the supply chain even without the resources to do so now.   In a new attempt to break free from relying on China and other countries for critical minerals, defence contractors will no longer be able to sell the Pentagon magnets, tantalum, or tungsten products that were mined, refined or separated in those four banned countries, even if the finished product was completed elsewhere.   Existing rules have allowed some raw materials from China as long as the final melting or production happens elsewhere.   The changes affect neodymium-iron-boron magnets used for electric vehicles, aerospace, and wind turbines. Samarium-cobalt magnets, tantalum metals and tungsten products vital to aerospace and defence because it is resistant to heat, will also be impacted by parallel restrictions.  The deadline threatens to expose a gap between Washington’s efforts to reduce its dependence on Chinese minerals and the industry’s ability to replace them. Despite millions of dollars in federal investment, the US lacks sufficient capacity across several stages of production, leaving manufacturers facing potential supply disruptions.  Long time coming   The restrictions stem from legislation introduced in 2019 targeting the Pentagon’s reliance on critical materials from countries of concern. Initial measures covered neodymium-iron-boron magnets, samarium-cobalt magnets and tungsten products were the first affected.  Every year since then restrictions grew tighter and encompassed more products, until the 2027 deadline was set in 2024.  President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14415 enforced the deadline and set out what will be expected from contractors. It requires supply chain mapping and due diligence, qualification of alternative supply sources and restricting available waivers under a prohibition on procuring certain critical metals and rare-earth magnets from countries of concern.  The tightening rules also extend beyond rare earth magnets. Gallium and germanium are next on the list to become subject to restrictions beginning Dec. 18, 2027.  Critical minerals security collides with decades-long mine timelines China controls most of the processing of these critical minerals and has also created restrictions of its own. The country introduced tighter restrictions on export controls on rare earths in April of 2025, which have been paused since October of that year. The suspension is set to lift on Jan. 10, 2027, just nine days after the US regulatory changes begin.  Investments to meet demand   The US has been making multi-million dollar investments in the sector since this new regulatory change was announced. While many projects and facilities are fully funded, they will not be ready to go into commercial production.  The issue still remains that mining capacity, separation capacity, metallization, and finished magnet production are four distinct steps that the US doesn’t have the capacity to complete yet.   The products can still fail the DFARS test if it passes through a covered country at any point throughout production, Environment and Energy Leader reported .   The US has been trying to engage with other countries that can become rare earths and other critical minerals suppliers, like Myanmar , Malaysia and Brazil .  While countries want to work together to reduce global reliance on China, there’s concerns around what role the US will play in the process. Brazil for example wants to develop the supply chain domestically rather than take the backseat in the critical minerals rush.  Lula’s Brazil win puts rare earths in Trump’s crosshairs The US has also been trying to develop its own infrastructure and supply chain domestically, funding a rare earth processing facility with ElementUSA and the Colorado School of Mines, and backing a Phoenix Tailings facility in New York state.   The only problem now is timing. With just 44 days remaining until the rules take effect, contractors face the immediate challenge of securing compliant materials from existing suppliers.

title: Copper price craters as AI, tariff trades unwind, wiping $186 billion off top producers in a month
zh_title: 随着人工智能和关税贸易的放松，铜价暴跌，一个月内就让顶级生产商损失了 1,860 亿美元
source: MINING.COM 全球矿业（稀土/关键矿产）
summary: 周三，铜价跌至 4 月份以来的最低点，原因是投机者放弃了与人工智能热潮相关的押注、美元飙升和美国关税前景黯淡，压倒了中国严重实物短缺的迹象，关键图表水平的损失加剧了抛售势头，拖累最大生产商的股价下跌 5% 至 9%。纽约最活跃合约Comex 12月交割铜，早盘尾盘跌幅高达6.7%至每磅5.5835美元（每吨12,309美元），创4月初以来最低水平，截至中午已有超过82,000份合约易手
content:
周三，铜价跌至 4 月份以来的最低点，原因是投机者放弃了与人工智能热潮相关的押注、美元飙升和美国关税前景黯淡，压倒了中国严重实物短缺的迹象，关键图表水平的损失加剧了抛售势头，拖累最大生产商的股价下跌 5% 至 9%。纽约最活跃合约Comex 12月交割的铜在早盘交易中下跌高达6.7%至每磅5.5835美元（每吨12,309美元），创4月初以来的最低水平，到中午已有超过82,000份合约易手。该合约已连续五个交易日下跌，当天的低点在三周内下跌了 16%，比 9 月 9 日创下的结算价 6.8885 美元低了 19%。2026 年峰值时 22% 的涨幅已被抹去，价格跌至去年年底的水平以下。据彭博社报道，伦敦金属交易所三个月期铜在官方交易中下跌 3.4%，至每吨 12,772.50 美元，随后跌幅扩大至 5.6%，为 4 月份以来的最低水平。在上海，交易量最大的合约下跌 3.4%，至每吨 97,920 元人民币（14,690 美元），而与人工智能硬件关系最密切的另一种金属锡，在伦敦下跌超过 7%，至近八个月来的最低水平。基础消费也无济于事。
据彭博社报道，摩科瑞金属和矿业研究主管尼古拉斯·斯诺登 (Nicholas Snowdon) 周三在上海举行的亚洲世界铜业会议上表示，“今天的铜需求更接近于衰退环境，而不是增长环境。”Natixis 分析师将美国库存和与人工智能相关的投资流相结合描述为泡沫，而银行对于 2027 年是否会出现短缺或过剩仍存在分歧。随着交易日的推移，矿商将抛售蔓延至股票。截至纽约下午早些时候，11 家最大的铜矿开采商总共损失了 490 亿美元，占其市值的 6% 以上，过去一周的损失达到 1,120 亿美元，过去一个月的损失达到 1,860 亿美元，即 20%。必和必拓市值下跌 6.5%，至 1780 亿美元，比一个月前减少 320 亿美元，远低于上周短暂反弹时的 2070 亿美元。南方铜业受到的打击最为严重，当日下跌 5.2%，一个月内下跌 26%，至 1,250 亿美元，损失 450 亿美元，使其 2026 年涨幅从 10 月中旬的 41% 降至 6%。自由港麦克莫兰铜金公司一个月前市值约为 1000 亿美元，下跌 6.7% 至 740 亿美元，今年几乎没有盈利。力拓 (Rio Tinto) 下跌 5.1%，至 1,300 亿美元；嘉能可 (Glencore) 下跌 6.5%，至 720 亿美元；英美资源集团 (Anglo American) 下跌 8.0%，泰克资源 (Teck Resources) 下跌 7.4%。
安托法加斯塔 (Antofagasta) 和伦丁矿业 (Lundin Mining) 是当日表现最差的大型矿业公司，均下跌超过 9%，并且与力拓 (Rio) 一起，目前在 2026 年都处于负值区域。在巴拿马就重启 Cobre巴拿马展开正式谈判后，第一量子矿业 (First Quantum Minerals) 周二股价上涨，下跌 5.5%，本月下跌 23%。艾芬豪矿业在一个月内下跌了 34%，到 2026 年下跌了 58%。盛宝银行大宗商品策略主管 Ole Hansen 向路透表示，由于通胀恐慌和融资成本上升的风险，投资者似乎放弃了几个技术水平的下跌，加剧了抛售势头。 “人工智能是一个触发器，但它并不是真正的驱动力，”他说。道明证券 (TD Securities) 高级大宗商品策略师瑞安·麦凯 (Ryan McKay) 将转向彭博社描述为一次彻底的重新调整

【原文 English Original】
Copper plunged to its lowest since April on Wednesday as speculators abandoned bets tied to the artificial intelligence boom, a surging dollar and fading US tariff prospects overwhelmed signs of acute physical shortage in China, and the loss of key chart levels added to momentum selling, dragging shares of the biggest producers down by between 5% and 9%. Comex copper for December delivery, the most active contract in New York, fell as much as 6.7% to $5.5835 a pound ($12,309 a tonne) in late morning trade, the lowest since early April, and more than 82,000 contracts had changed hands by midday. The contract has fallen for five sessions in a row and at the day’s low was down 16% in three weeks and 19% below the record settlement of $6.8885 reached on September 9. A gain for 2026 that stood at 22% at the peak has been wiped out, with the price dipping below where it ended last year. On the London Metal Exchange, three-month copper was down 3.4% at $12,772.50 a tonne in official trading and later extended its loss to as much as 5.6%, the lowest since April, Bloomberg reports. In Shanghai the most-traded contract shed 3.4% to 97,920 yuan ($14,690) a tonne, and tin, the other metal most closely tied to AI hardware, slumped more than 7% in London to its lowest in almost eight months. Underlying consumption is not helping either. “Copper demand today is closer to a recessionary-like environment than growth environment,” Nicholas Snowdon, head of metals and mining research at Mercuria, told the World Copper Conference Asia in Shanghai on Wednesday, according to Bloomberg. Natixis analysts have described the combination of US stockpiling and AI-linked investment flows as a bubble, while banks remain split on whether 2027 brings shortage or surplus . Miners routed The selling spread to equities as the session wore on. Eleven of the largest copper-exposed miners lost a combined $49 billion, or more than 6% of their market value, by early afternoon in New York, taking their losses to $112 billion over the past week and $186 billion, or 20%, over the past month. BHP dropped 6.5% to a market value of $178 billion, $32 billion less than a month ago and well under the $207 billion it was worth during last week’s short-lived bounce . Southern Copper has been hit hardest among the majors, down 5.2% on the day and 26% in a month to $125 billion, a loss of $45 billion that has cut its 2026 gain to 6% from 41% in mid-October. Freeport-McMoRan, worth about $100 billion a month ago, fell 6.7% to $74 billion and is barely positive for the year. Rio Tinto lost 5.1% to $130 billion and Glencore 6.5% to $72 billion, while Anglo American fell 8.0% and Teck Resources 7.4%. Antofagasta and Lundin Mining were the day’s worst performers among the larger names, both down more than 9%, and along with Rio are now in negative territory for 2026. First Quantum Minerals, which jumped on Tuesday after Panama opened formal talks on restarting Cobre Panama , fell 5.5% and is 23% lower over the month. Ivanhoe Mines has shed 34% in a month and 58% in 2026. Towel thrown in Investors appear to be giving up after the loss of several technical levels added to momentum selling, Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, told Reuters, pointing to an inflation scare and the risk of higher funding costs. “AI was a trigger, but it’s not really the driver,” he said. Ryan McKay, senior commodity strategist at TD Securities, described the move to Bloomberg as a complete recalibration of the copper market: worries about Federal Reserve tightening are weighing on the demand outlook, the midterm results have dented optimism about AI spending, and the New York premium over London, a proxy for tariff expectations, is narrowing. Speculative positioning has largely unwound and in places flipped net short, while selling by trend-following funds has accelerated the decline, McKay said. Tech stocks steadied on Wednesday after Nvidia reported a 103% jump in quarterly revenue to $115.8 billion late on Tuesday, the chipmaker’s first results since Jensen Huang’s exit rattled the metals demand story , but that did nothing for copper. The dollar is holding near a 19-month high ahead of the release of minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting, at which two officials voted for another rate increase. Sentiment took a further knock late on Tuesday when Stan Druckenmiller, among the best-known backers of copper’s AI trade, told a conference in Austin he is now short the metal. A filing earlier in the week showed his family office had sold out of Southern Copper and bought gold miners during the third quarter. Druckenmiller exits copper, steel and chip stocks to buy gold miners Fund positioning has already been cut hard.
